News.title: ‘Extremely significant’ car bomb ‘being driven across NI border’ intercepted as woman, 20s, & man, 40s, lifted
News.content:
TWO people are being questioned after gardai foiled an alleged cross-border bomb plot in Northern Ireland this week.

The explosive device was found in a vehicle during a major operation near Carrickmacross, Co Monaghan last Wednesday.

Gardai believe the device was being driven across the border for an attack in Northern Ireland.

The search was part of an operation by the Special Detective Unit targeting dissident republican activity.





Gardai stopped the vehicle travelling south of Carrickmacross on the busy N2 road at around 3pm on Wednesday.

The Army Bomb Disposal team was called to the scene to make the device safe before it was removed for a forensic examination.

Gardai said the bomb had been fully assembled and was ready to use.

The driver of the car, a woman in her 20s, was arrested at the scene and is being detained under Section 30 of the Offences Against the State Act.



A man in his 40s has since also been arrested and can be questioned for up to three days under the same legislation.

Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly confirmed details of the operation as he spoke to media at a Garda graduation event in Co Tipperary today.

He said: “To be clear, what we found was an extremely significant seizure.

“So this was an explosive device.”

News.title: Shocking moment car flips over and barrel rolls across pavement into cyclist as three taken to hospital
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a car flips onto its side and slams into a cyclist as he rode along a pavement.

Horror CCTV shows the white Renault Captur suddenly leave the road before barrel-rolling across the pavement and crashing into the rider.



Just seconds earlier, another cyclist had passed through the exact same spot, narrowly avoiding the smash.

The crash happened just before 4.45pm on Tuesday on Dormers Wells Lane at the junction with Telford Road in Southall, west London.



The footage, captured on a home’s CCTV camera – just metres from two school’s – shows the Renault veer off the road before overturning and sliding.

The cyclist has no time to react before he is struck by the out-of-control car hurtling towards him.



The Renault eventually comes to rest on its side and wedged against a lamppost.

Miraculously, nobody was killed, although three people were taken to hospital after the crash.



Shocked witnesses rushed to help the occupants of the car and the cyclist before emergency services arrived.

A London Ambulance Service spokesperson said: “We were called at 4:43pm Tuesday 21 July to reports of a road traffic collision on Telford Road, Southall, UB1.

“We sent resources to the scene including ambulance crews, an advanced paramedic and an incident response officer.

“We treated three patients at the scene.

“One patient was taken to a major trauma centre as a priority, one to a local hospital and the third patient was discharged at the scene”.



Locals were left stunned by the dramatic footage.

Margatet Wittich said: “Oh my God.

“How do you do that? A miracle that all are okay.”

Amrit Grewal said: “The second cyclist narrowly missed it.”

Vik Singh added: “How fast was he going?”



Another person wrote: “Like how do you explain that?

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Like how.”

The Met Police has been approached for comment.

News.title: Shocking moment vile driver films himself drinking whiskey while speeding before killing girl, 12, in horror crash
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a driver films himself speeding and drinking whiskey behind the wheel just weeks before he ploughed into a family car and killed a schoolgirl.

Shocking footage shows Jordan Kenyon, 31, swigging Jack Daniels and steering with his knees as he veers across double white lines towards an oncoming 4×4.



In the disturbing clip, Kenyon boasts he is the “best f***ing designated drunk driver in the world” as he speeds along the highway.

Weeks later, while high on drugs and doing 95mph, Kenyon ploughed into a family car – killing Mia Rossiter, 12, and seriously injuring her mum, dad and little sister.



He showed little remorse following the crash as he lit up a cigarette and later told cops he hadn’t been driving.

Kenyon, who has never held a driving licence and was on bail wearing an ankle monitor at the time, has now pleaded guilty to culpable driving causing death.



A judge branded Kenyon’s reckless driving as a game of “Russian Roulette”, telling Geelong County Court that “it was a matter of time before he killed”.

“This family sitting here today could have been any other family,” he added.

Kenyon was travelling on the Hamilton Highway in Stonehaven, 10km west of Geelong, on January 3, 2024, when he hit the Rossiter family’s car head-on.

Mia, described in court as a kind-hearted little girl, died at the scene.



The court heard Kenyon was “off his face” on the drug GHB and had fallen asleep at the wheel in the moments before the crash.

He had also breached his bail conditions numerous times in the run-up to the tragedy, despite wearing the ankle monitor.

In other videos posted online, Kenyon can be seen showing off the bracelet while whinging about “how hard it is to make it in society”.



Speaking outside court, Mia’s devastated mum Danica Rossiter described her daughter as “the light of my life”.

“I don’t wish this on anyone. I don’t hate many people but there’s no words for the amount of hate I have for him,” she said.

The court also heard Kenyon has a long history of dangerous driving.

In 2019 he was jailed for six years after stealing a car and driving at speeds of up to 105mph in a police pursuit.

Kenyon has pleaded guilty to culpable driving causing death, reckless conduct endangering life and two counts of negligently causing serious injury.



He will be sentenced next Thursday and faces a maximum of 20 years behind bars.

News.title: Can you use an outside tap during a hosepipe ban? The three ways to rescue your garden this summer
News.content:
OVER 23million Brits are currently under temporary hosepipe ban restrictions around the country.

After weeks of hot weather and dry conditions, many may be uncertain how to rescue their garden without a hose.



Eight water providers across England and Wales have introduced hosepipe bans this month, with Thames Water‘s over 10million customers coming under a ban yesterday.

Under the rules, a hosepipe cannot be used for a number of garden activities, such as watering plants, filling up swimming and paddling pools, and cleaning cars.



Anyone caught breaking the rules could be slammed with a £1,000 fine, unless there is an exemption, or suitable loophole.

For gardeners, this can include being able to water newly-laid turf for four weeks after it is installed, watering new saplings and trees, or using recycled water.

A hosepipe is not the only piece of equipment that is restricted by a ban -sprinklers and pressures also cannot be used when rules are enforced.

Despite a number of items being unusuable in the garden this summer, the use of an outdoor tap can be a helpful alternative.

During a hosepipe ban, there is no rule preventing the use of an outside tap – however, as expected, it cannot be used to supply a hosepipe.

An outside tap can be used to fill up both a watering can or a bucket, which is completely permitted during a hosepipe ban.



There are also no restrictions on the size of the container used to water plants, so a watering can and bucket can be as big as you like.

Approved drip or trickle irrigation systems can also be used to water plants, but they must meet the specific criteria of having a reducing valve or timer.

Hosepipe ban rules - what you can't use a hose for The rules of a hosepipe ban: No watering gardens using hoses or sprinklers

No cleaning cars, boats or other motor vehicles

No watering plants on domestic land

No filling or maintaining domestic swimming or paddling pools

No filling domestic ponds or fountains

No cleaning outdoor surfaces like patios, walls or paths

Various loopholes can also let you use a hosepipe to fill up a fish pond , clean large animals and provide them with drinking water.

It is important to check the website of your individual water supplier before using these loopholes, as some providers have slightly different rules and regulations.

News.title: Tourists warned to stay away from ‘hidden’ UK blue lagoon made famous on TikTok during Covid pandemic
News.content:
TOURISTS have been urged to “stay away” from a lush beauty spot that features a hidden blue lagoon.

The area became a TikTok sensation six years ago during the Covid pandemic.



Brombil Reservoir, in South Wales, is known as the hidden oasis of the region, with crystal blue waters and vibrant green hills.

Located in a 100ft deep valley on Margam mountain, its secluded position has drawn in visitors from across the world, who hope to catch a glimpse of this natural Welsh gem.



But now, tourists have been warned to stay away from the area, following overwhelming visitor numbers and concerns of people swimming at the site.

Leisure Estate Investments – which has owned the reservoir since 2024 – even introduced a £2 charge per visit as a “temporary deterrent”, as well as installing barriers on its dam face.

Complaints include issues with traffic and littering, with reports of visitors fly-tipping, trespassing and damaging structures around the site.

The reservoir is a former 19th Century colliery that was flooded and repurposed to supply water to Port Talbot Docks.

The area remains “vital” for flood protection and has a “unique ecosystem” that is currently suffering as a result of the rubbish left on the site.

Reports of visitors paddleboarding and walking along the dam face also pose “inherent safety risks”, given the depth and exceptionally cold temperature of the water.



A spokesperson for the company told the BBC: “We have strictly banned [people] from going there and walking on the face of the dam.

“Our long-term vision has always been to build a sustainable public-private framework so the community can safely enjoy this asset.”

News.title: Shocking moment 2 ‘drunken’ Brit soldiers smash through cars after ‘stealing’ 15-tonne tank & rampaging through streets
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment an allegedly drunk soldier stole a “tank” and smashed up civilian cars in a £100,000 joyride around camp.

Two engineers were arrested after the 15 ton Bulldog vehicle was filmed on a destruction derby.



Pals said the troops went boozing off base before returning at around 1am this morning and stealing the tracked armoured vehicle.

The Fast and Furious style rampage took place in Swinton Barracks on Perham Down – which is part of the Tidworth Garrison and home of 26 Engineer Regiment.



A tanked up sapper floored the accelerator to hit the Bulldog’s top speed of 32mph.

The armoured personnel carrier – which needs a minimum crew of two – is powered by a formidable 240hp Rolls Royce engine.

The driver struggled to keep the Bulldog straight as it thundered down a narrow access road lined with soldiers’ personal cars.

Several vehicles were damaged as the tank made its way along the street – with two completely wrecked by the massive 15-tonne armoured vehicle.



The Bulldog is more than 9ft wide and 17ft long and designed to move troops over boggy battlefields.

Footage of the joyride shows a pimped up Vauxhall panel van and a silver SUV crumpled and skewed after Bulldog smashed into them.

The tank can be seen speeding off along the street as a shocked onlooker films from a window.

A trail of destruction is left in the wake of the tank as the soldiers carried out their destructive joyride.



Miraculously no one was hurt – and unsurprisingly the Bulldog was also undamaged.

The Sun understands the SUV was a Chinese made MG ZS electric vehicle – worth around £30,000 – which soldiers have been warned not to hold sensitive conversations inside due to risk of spying.

The drunken soldier then parked the Bulldog neatly in a parking bay before calmly returning to his barracks.

Images show the massive armoured vehicle slotted neatly in a parking spot, with cars around it left undamaged.



The soldier responsible for the joyride was nicked in his room by Royal Military Police at dawn as comrades discovered the devastation on camp.

A second soldier was also arrested.

The Army lists driving as one of 26 Engineer Regt’s specialist roles.

An Army spokesperson said: “We expect the highest standards from our personnel.

“Two soldiers have been arrested by the Royal Military Police following an incident at Perham Down this morning, 24th July.



“We will not comment further while an investigation is ongoing.”

News.title: Brit ‘drug mule’ jailed for 9 years after being caught on camera with suitcases stuffed with cannabis in £280k plot
News.content:
A BRITISH drug mule has been jailed for nearly ten years in Turkey after a sniffer dog detected £300,000 of cannabis in his suitcase.

Taylor Johnson, 20, was arrested at Istanbul airport as he caught a connecting flight to the UK on the way home from holiday in Thailand with his girlfriend.



Customs officers found 19kg of cannabis in 17 black, vacuum-packed bags.

Johnson said he had agreed to bring the bag back for a man back in the UK who had threatened him and claimed he had no idea it contained drugs.



But a court in Istanbul has now jailed him for nine years and two months.

He is serving his sentence in an overcrowded maximum security facility in the Asian half of the city as his lawyers begin the process of trying to get him transferred to a UK jail.



His lawyer Bilgehan Berk told The Sun: “This is a very positive outcome for Taylor as the 19kg was considered a very large quantity.

“The courts are generally inclined to hand down sentences of around 12 to 13 years, but when they’re this young, we usually manage to persuade them to impose a lower sentence.

“He’ll stay some time here first, but then he’ll apply to be transferred to his home country.

“There won’t be an appeal.



“The prosecutor accepted that this was transit transportation of narcotics, rather than importation of narcotics into Turkey.

“Had they been imported, the sentence would have started at 20 years.”

Johnson had gone on holiday to Thailand with girlfriend Holly Cooper, 20, in April.



He later told police that a man in the UK threatened him and demanded money after they had been involved in a road accident.

On the last night of their holiday, a Chinese man delivered a black suitcase to the couple’s hotel and Johnson brought it home with him.

He managed to check it in at Bangkok without being detected but after they landed at Istanbul to catch their connecting flight to England a drugs dog checked their luggage and found the drugs.

A video exclusively obtained by The Sun showed the investigators opening the suitcase and finding the cannabis, worth around £280,000.

Care worker Holly, of Coseley, and Johnson, of Wednesbury, both West Midlands, were arrested on suspicion of “manufacturing and trafficking narcotic or psychotropic substances” and taken to different prisons.



No drugs were found in Holly’s bag and she was allowed to return to the UK and was today acquitted.

Speaking through an interpreter, jobless Johnson told Gaziosmanpaşa criminal court at an earlier hearing: “The person involved in the accident had obtained my details.

“About a week later, he began threatening both me and my family. He demanded £3,000 from me.



“I told him I did not have the money. He then instructed me to travel to Thailand and bring back an item located there to the United Kingdom.

“He told me it was a specially designed suitcase, so I did not know it contained drugs.

“I then called my girlfriend and told her I was going to Thailand on holiday, asking whether she wanted to come with me. She agreed. Everyone paid for their own ticket.

“Holly had absolutely no knowledge of what was happening. When we arrived in Thailand, the person who had sent me there called me one night from the UK. Holly was asleep at the time.

“He told me that the suitcase was ready at the reception desk and that I needed to collect it. I picked up the suitcase. It was locked.



“I then travelled to Turkey on my way back to the UK with that suitcase. I only learned what was inside the suitcase when I arrived in Turkey.”

He added: “I apologise. Had I known that the suitcase contained drugs, I would never have done such a thing.”

Holly said at the same hearing: “Taylor never told me that anyone had forced him to go to Thailand.

“I genuinely believed we were there on holiday. We were only transiting through Turkey on our way back from Thailand. I had no knowledge of what was inside the suitcase.”

Johnson is in Maltepe Prison with around 15 other Brits in a dormitory for 40 foreign inmates.



Human rights inspectors have found severe overcrowding and poor living conditions at the jail.

Wards designed for 28 inmates are crammed with 40, with some forced to sleep on the floor.

The couple’s families back home in the UK were said to be “in bits” at the Midnight Express-style horror which their children found themselves in.

The 1978 hit movie featured a student who was thrown in a Turkish hell-hole prison after trying to smuggle drugs out of the country.

A family friend said at the time of Taylor’s arrest that he was a “good kid” who had been groomed by a trafficking gang to bring back the drugs.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The friend added: “I have seen Taylor grow up. He’s a good, happy kid.

“Everyone makes mistakes.”

A Foreign Office spokesperson said: “We are supporting a British national detained in Turkey and are in contact with the local authorities.”

News.title: Toddler dies after getting head trapped behind a mirror at nursery ‘while staff partied during birthday celebration’
News.content:
NURSERY HORROR Toddler dies after getting head trapped behind a mirror at nursery ‘while staff partied during birthday celebration’

A one-year-old boy has died after becoming trapped behind a nursery mirror while staff allegedly partied at a birthday celebration.

Tragedy struck at the Luz do Bras childcare centre in the Bras district of Sao Paulo, Brazil‘s largest city, on Wednesday.



Abdoulaye Dieng was in a playroom with other children when his head slipped into the gap between a metal safety bar protecting a mirror and the wall.

Horrifying security camera footage showed the toddler desperately trying to free himself for six agonising minutes.



After noticing he was trapped, nursery workers managed to prise him from the gap, according to the Civil Police investigation.

Military Police officers on patrol were approached by childcare staff at around 9.20am.



Employees had scrambled out of the nursery carrying the unconscious child in their arms.

Abdoulaye was rushed to Mooca Emergency Care Unit but was later pronounced dead.

Abdoulaye’s father, Ibrahima Dieng said he dropped his son at the nursery at about 7.30am.

But just 90 minutes later the Senegalese street vendor, who has lived in Brazil for eight years, said he received a phone call telling him the boy was involved in an accident.



He said: “I went to the school and asked, ‘Where is my child?’ They told me to wait, and then they said he had died.

“We have to cry, cry so much. It’s heart-breaking.”

He added that Abdoulaye’s mother became ill after receiving the news and that the family had been left shattered by the loss.

Police launched a fresh line of inquiry after receiving allegations that the children may have been left unsupervised.



Nursery employees were allegedly enjoying a birthday celebration when the accident happened.

Investigators seized the nursery’s CCTV footage to establish whether staff were absent from the room at the time.

Police said witness statements indicated the gathering took place before the tragedy.

The case has been registered as suspected negligent homicide – meaning there is no allegation of intent to kill.



Five members of staff, including coordinators, the director and teaching staff, are under investigation.

The family’s lawyer, Erson de Oliveira, said: “What we were told is that the child was playing without supervision.

“He trapped his head in the metal bar holding the mirror and suffocated without anyone helping him until he died.”

The CCTV footage appeared to support concerns the toddler was left without proper supervision, the lawyer said.



Oliveira added: “Just as he managed to put his head into the gap, someone could have lifted his little body and easily pulled him free if they had been there. That help never came.”

Oliveira also questioned why nursery staff took the child to hospital themselves instead of immediately calling an ambulance or the fire brigade.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Other parents told Brazilian media they had previously complained about an alleged lack of staff at the nursery.

One mother claimed a single teacher was sometimes left looking after between 12 and 15 children.

News.title: 'Extremely significant' car bomb intercepted by police on Irish border
News.content:
'Extremely significant' car bomb intercepted by police on Irish border

A woman in her 20s was arrested by Garda after the 'extremely significant' explosive device was found in a vehicle near the Irish border

View Image

An “extremely significant” bomb has been intercepted in a vehicle in transit near the Irish border in an operation targeting dissident republicans, gardaí have said.

‌



In an intelligence-led swoop, members of the Garda’s Special Detective Unit stopped the vehicle travelling on the N2 south of Carrickmacross, Co Monaghan on Wednesday afternoon.

‌



It is understood the device found contained suspected military grade explosives, with Garda sources describing the bomb as “highly sophisticated” and “advanced”.

‌



The vehicle’s female driver, aged in her 20s, was arrested at the scene and remained in Garda custody on Friday. Another suspect, a man aged in his 40s, has since been arrested and is being held at a Garda station in the Dublin area.

Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly confirmed details of the operation as he spoke to media at a Garda graduation event in Co Tipperary on Friday. “To be clear, what we found was an extremely significant seizure,” he said. “So this was an explosive device.”

‌



Speaking to reporters in Co Tipperary, he said: “Any seizure of this nature is really concerning."

“However, we certainly know that there are a small minority of dissident republicans who did not agree with the Good Friday Agreement, they did not put weapons and explosives (out of use), they didn’t, you know, go through with the proper process in relation to decommissioning. So that is something that we continue to deal with.

“There’s a small minority of these individuals, I would describe them as radicalised republicans, and this is a threat that we’re going to continue to face for some time in An Garda Síochána.

Article continues below

“We work very closely with our colleagues in PSNI (Police Service of Northern Ireland) and the intelligence services in the UK to deal with this threat. But I want to commend the members of An Garda Síochána who are involved in this operation.”

News.title: Andy Burnham opens No10 North, describing it as 'nerve centre of rewired Britain'
News.content:
Andy Burnham opens No10 North, describing it as 'nerve centre of rewired Britain'

Addressing staff at No10 North, Andy Burnham said the new office in Manchester will be 'the nerve centre of a rewired Britain' and sadi power and energy will flow through the site in the coming years

View 5 Images Andy Burnham at the opening of No10 North in Manchester (Image: James Speakman/The Times/PA Wire)

Andy Burnham has pledged the newly-opened No10 North will be "the nerve centre of a rewired Britain".

‌



In an address to staff at the office in Manchester - which became operational this week - he said power and energy will flow through the site, where he plans to work at least one day a week.

‌



Mr Burnham announced the new office would be set up to balance the concentration of power in London - and said its impact is more profound than most have realised so far. He said: "Isn't it better that we have a North Pole, that balances the South Pole of our country where power will always be concentrated? But at least it creates that sense of a more balanced country, and that big things can be done from here.

‌



Angela Rayner rules out rent controls as she admits 1.5million home pledge getting harder to meet READ MORE :

View 5 Images The PM said the site would be Britain's 'nerve centre' (Image: James Speakman/The Times/PA Wire)

"This is the place where Whitehall meets the rest of the country, I've called it the nerve centre for a rewired Britain. Or if you think about it in terms of the day-to-day kind of challenge around growth, it will be the situation room for growth where we all get around the table - Mayors with all of the teams and the Whitehall departments - so we get those decisions made more quickly.

"We break through the logjams and we get things done. So it is much more profound, I think, than people have worked out so far. It's not just a new office. Through this place power is going to flow, energy is going to flow."

‌



Mr Burnham announced his intention to set up a base of power in Manchester, where he was regional mayor for nearly a decade, before becoming PM. He seeing No10 North in operation was the best day of his life.

The PM hit back at sceptics arguing other parts of the country would still feel left out, saying: "No10 North is as much for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland as it is for the regions of England. if you get that feeling, then I think so much is possible. That doesn't feel possible right now. And we can really get the energy, flowing right around the country."

View 5 Images Police outside the building, home to security service GCHQ (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

‌



The government faces questions about the cost of setting up the operation in the North. Hitting back at critics, Mr Burnham said: "There'll be many voices out there, I can hear them all already, often London based, but not exclusively... They like to say, `Oh, this will just be the new levelling up, or another sort of short-lived gimmick', and they'll also say `What's it going to cost?'"

He continued: "What does it cost for everybody to troop down to London every time there's a meeting when you need to make an argument about something?

"What does that cost? So actually, isn't it better that we have a North Pole that balances the South Pole of our country, where power will always be concentrated?

‌



"At least it creates that sense of a more balanced country, and that big things can be done from here."

View 5 Images Mr Burnham arriving at No10 North on Friday morning (Image: James Speakman/The Times/PA Wire)

Cabinet members including Chancellor John Healey were at No10 North for a meeting of the National Economic Council, which Mr Burnham says will drive growth across the country. Also present were Cabinet ministers Angela Rayner, Yvette Cooper, Jonathan Reynolds and Louise Haigh.

‌



The Prime Minister recounted having to leave the area he grew up in because there were no jobs, saying No10 North was about resetting this. The PM stated: "It's true of places all over the country to get on in life, you had to leave where you were, because things weren't here.

"And the country has always been a little like that, hasn't it? That opportunity is not being evenly spread around the country, and not all places have felt that they're part of the national story. And that is what this government is going to work every single day to change. And that is what No10 North is all about."

View 5 Images First Secretary of State Louise Haigh arriving at No10 North (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

There was a large-scale police presence outside the building - home of intelligence service GCHQ - as the Prime Minister arrived.

Housing Secretary Ms Rayner, who returned to the Cabinet on Tuesday, said: "The principle and the culture that he set in is that power pushed down through the devolution agenda has given benefits to Greater Manchester, that every other area should have the same, and they should be able to reap the benefits of that.

"And this is about making sure that people can see this is not about holding power in Westminster. This is about pushing power down, having respect for mayors, having respect for local leaders, working with economists in the local area and just driving that agenda forward."

News.title: Thrill seekers clamber off famous Blackpool Pleasure Beach ride amid 'derailment' fear
News.content:
Thrill seekers clamber off famous Blackpool Pleasure Beach ride amid 'derailment' fear

The Big Dipper, one the the oldest rollercoaster's in the world at Blackpool Pleasure Beach, has been halted with an investigation underway amid claims it derailed

View Image (Image: Supplied)

Thrill seekers have been forced to evacuate a famous ride at Blackpool Pleasure Beach following fears it was about to derail.

‌



The Big Dipper, one the the oldest rollercoasters in the world, at the Pleasure Beach resort in Blackpool came to a "stop" at around 2pm yesterday (July 23).

‌



Footage on social media appears to show broken wooden slats in between the rails with comments that there was a derailment on the Big Dipper.

‌



And Pleasure Beach Resort has now confirmed the closure of the ride while an investigation takes place into what happened and clarified that the carriages came to a halt rather than coming off the ride.

A spokesperson from Pleasure Beach Resort told LancsLive: “The Big Dipper came to a stop Thursday July 23, around 2pm, at a very low point in the ride.

‌



“Following this, a manual deboarding took place with guests guided safely by trained operators. All riders were checked by first aid trained staff, with no injuries reported. An internal investigation is taking place to determine the root cause.” They did not address claims of damage to the track and it is not clear for how long the ride will not be operating.

Many people took to social media to comment on the derailment claims. "We were there on Monday and they were putting in new planks in which the track sits on just at the bottom on the drop," wrote one person, while another said: "The back carriages have always been rough and feel like it flips a bit in some parts."

A further comment read: "Was on the ride on Saturday and was a little rough but nothing out of the ordinary if anything the Grand National was worse, genuinely thought at times the train might 'jump the track' but got back to the station with no issues, hope this gets sorted."

Article continues below

While another person said: "They’ve spent a lot of time working on that lately and it’s not long opened. Hopefully they can sort it but who knows how long Big Dipper has left."

Meanwhile, Blackpool Pleasure Beach has been ranked as the top UK destination on a global list for places to keep children entertained on holiday by Attraction Tickets. With the summer holidays about to start it has been named sixth in the international list with Disney and Universal taking the top spots.

News.title: Anyone who spots stray cats on holiday urged to do one thing
News.content:
Anyone who spots stray cats on holiday urged to do one thing

An animal welfare charity has shared advice for holidaymakers who find stray animals

View 2 Images The animal charity has shared advice for cat lovers (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

The RSPCA has shared advice for any travellers worried about stray cats they spot on holiday. The animal welfare charity has urged people to do one thing in such a situation.

‌



The experts explained that it's important to check if cats look underfed or unwell. In a Facebook post, the charity explained: "It's common to see street cats while on holiday abroad, but not all cats may need our intervention, and it's important to know how to help them responsibly, wherever you may be this summer."

‌



The post was accompanied by a video. In the clip, an RSPCA staff member explained exactly what holidaymakers can do to help stray animals. She told viewers: "Here's how you can help stray cats abroad this summer. It can be tempting to wish to help cats whilst overseas, but not all cats need our help. Do they look skinny or unwell? Or do they look quite well fed?

‌



"You can also check if the cat has had its ears clipped, and what that means is that the cat has been caught, neutered, and then rereleased back into the area."

The expert continued: "What you can also do is speak to the local people in the area, who may be able to let you know the organisations, or individuals out there, currently caring for the cats. You may also find that at your local gift shop, at your resort, there is actually cat food in there, and that's to encourage tourists to buy the cat food and feed the cats.

‌



"What you may also be able to do is make a donation. This donation will probably go towards maybe treatment or even the trap, neuter, and release programme."

Holidaymakers could also write to tourism boards or public officials. For instance, people could send a letter encouraging the local authority to offer their help, the RSPCA said.

"You could even write to those in power, or even tourist boards. You could explain that you love visiting their country, but were sad to see so many cats in need of help, and would love to see an investment into that line of work in the future."

Article continues below

View 2 Images Holidaymakers are urged to help responsibly (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

In the video's caption, the RSPCA encouraged animal lovers to 'share this advice with fellow holiday-goers and check out International Cat Care for more information.' International Cat Care is a global charity. The charity's website reiterates that cat lovers can help by finding out who is already helping in the area they are visiting.

It said: "Ask about the local people or organisations who are working in the area. There may be individuals, charities, local municipality activity or non-government organisations (NGOs) working in the area to help the cats."

News.title: Hosepipe ban already impacting millions could be extended - check if your area has restrictions
News.content:
Hosepipe ban already impacting millions could be extended - check if your area has restrictions

In some areas affected by the hosepipe ban from one of the main firms, your water may be supplied by a different local provider where restrictions do not apply.

View 3 Images Check whether your area is under a hosepipe ban (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Hosepipe bans affecting millions of people could be extended even further this summer - and our map reveals all the areas currently under restrictions.

‌



The National Drought Group has warned that more parts of southern, central, and eastern England are at risk of the same conditions as more than a dozen other areas across the country. Seven water companies, including some of the country's biggest providers such as Thames Water, Southern Water, and Southeast Water, have been forced to impose restrictions due to weeks without a single drop of rain in some areas.

‌



The NDG has revealed which areas are currently in the critical stage before official drought, “prolonged dry weather”, and just a small step away from the strictest water controls.

‌



View 3 Images Thames Water imposed restrictions to hosepipes (Image: Getty Images)

The NDG, which convened on Monday following 12 consecutive days of temperatures above 30C, counts members from across the UK's environmental network amongst its ranks, including the Government and Met Office. They concluded that 13 areas are currently in the "prolonged dry weather" stage.

They include: The aforementioned areas fall under the jurisdiction of several different water companies, including Affinity Water, SES Water and Wessex Water, and could see potentially millions more people placed under hosepipe bans. Currently, temporary use bans have been extended for 23 million customers across the UK in a bid to protect the environment and reduce strain on vital networks, reports the Mirror.

‌



Areas currently under a hosepipe ban include: East Anglia

West Midlands

Devon

Cornwall

Isles of Scilly

Lincolnshire

Northamptonshire

Hertfordshire

London

Wessex

Thames

Solent

South Downs

Whether it applies to you depends on your water provider. In some areas under a ban from one of the main firms, your water may be supplied by a different local provider where restrictions do not apply.

Use our interactive map below to check whether your area is under a hosepipe ban:

‌



The latest available data from the Environment Agency, a recent snapshot taken between July 2 and 15, shows an average of zero rainfall across its weather stations in central and southeastern England over 14 consecutive days. The alarming figures represent the longest unbroken period of no rainfall in southeast England since April 1997, when there was no rainfall for 15 days.

In central England, the record was set back in 1996, more than 30 years ago, with another 14-day stretch without a single drop of recorded rainfall. Helen Wakeham, Chair of the National Drought Group and Director of Water at the Environment Agency, said the astonishing lack of rainfall is having a profound effect across the UK's industries.

‌



She said: “Dry weather depletes our water, while the hot conditions mean we use more of it. This is a difficult combination, and we are seeing the effects on our farmers, our wildlife, and the amount available for public and business use.

“All sectors are taking action, and we are grateful to the public for following the restrictions, where in place, to make sure there is enough water for everyone this summer. We want everyone to stay safe and hydrated during the hot weather but every drop we can save is a drop more for nature and agriculture.”

View 3 Images A road closed in Windsor town centre in Berkshire due to works by Thames Water. (Image: Maureen McLean/Shutterstock)

‌



That prolonged absence of rainfall looks set to continue in the coming days, with high pressure expected to remain the dominant force for at least the next five days.

Only coastal areas and southeast England, and possibly northern Scotland, could see some rainfall during this period, with mid-week showers possible before weather fronts attempt to push in from the northwest. Much of that rain, however, is likely to fall over Northern Ireland and Scotland.

Will Lang, Chief Meteorologist at the Met Office, said: “Much of England has experienced a notably warm and dry first half of summer, with July particularly dry and some locations recording little or no rainfall so far this month. The UK has already seen three heatwaves in 2026 and, while some rain is possible at times, the overall outlook remains for largely settled conditions.”

Article continues below

In the last two weeks, Affinity Water, Anglian Water, Cambridge Water, Southern Water, South East Water, Thames Water, and South West Water have announced Temporary Use Bans (TUB) across either all or part of their region. Hosepipes are restricted, but watering cans and buckets can still be used. If people with disabilities or health conditions live in an area covered by a TUB, they can contact their local water company about their situation.

A hosepipe can use 1,000 litres an hour, which is more than a family of four will use in a day. Restrictions on their use form an essential part of drought planning, and recent research found most people support a ban if there is a compelling reason.

David Henderson, Water UK Chief Executive, said: “The last thing water companies want to do is restrict the amount of water people can use, but demand is at unprecedented levels following the warmest spring and June on record.”

News.title: Mum and daughter drowned at Mersea Island beach in 'tragedy waiting to happen'
News.content:
Mum and daughter drowned at Mersea Island beach in 'tragedy waiting to happen'

A tragic double drowning that claimed the lives of a mum and her 15-year-old daughter happened on the same beach where a 30-year-old dad previously died while saving the life of his three-year-old son

Interview with family friend of a 15-year-old girl and her mother who died trying to save a seven-year-old relative on West Mersea beach.

Local residents near a beach where a mum and a daughter drowned on a doomed day trip have told the Mirror it was a 'tragedy waiting to happen'.

‌



Samiha Rahman, 15, and her mother Shally Rahman, 41, from Ilford, London, died after getting into difficulty at West Mersea Beach on Mersea Island, Essex on Wednesday night.

‌



The pair were "not very good swimmers" and were just on a "day out" at the beach, a family friend said.

‌



Essex Police said officers were called by the ambulance service at 5.35pm on Wednesday after reports that several people had got into difficulty in the water.

View 4 Images Samiha Rahman, 15, died while trying to save her seven-year-old cousin

The force has since confirmed that the mother and daughter, from London, were believed to be trying to help a seven-year-old relative, who is in hospital in a critical condition. Two others were rescued at the scene.

‌



It follows a previous drowning in 2023 and years of local concerns over whether enough warnings and safety measures are in place along the beach.

'Suddenly a big wave came'

Eyewitnesses said the group were on a sandbank when the tide came in "very quickly", leaving several people in the water.

Speaking to the BBC, Shally Rahman’s brother in law, Matiur Rahman, said about 10 members of his extended family were near the water playing when "suddenly a big wave came".

‌



Mr Rahman said: "My whole family – we are speechless. We can’t believe what we heard from my brother.

"We are very shocked."

The East of England Ambulance Service initially said that one patient was transported by air and three taken by road to hospital after the incident in the water near Sea View Holiday Park.

‌



View 4 Images Shally Rahman, 41, was pronounced dead along with her daughter

Locals come to the rescue

Local people raced to help the family after hearing a "commotion" on the beach - including one man who reportedly pulled several people from the water, and a group of three teenage waitresses who were among the first on the scene.

Describing the efforts of her great-niece Leonie Powling, 19, and 18-year-old friend Keira French, Seaview Beach Diner owner Melanie Shuker, 64, said: "The girls had heard people shouting for help on the beach. Two girls ran into the café, quite hysterical, and asked if anybody could help them. All four of the girls here, aged 16 to 19, went to the water's edge where a man had pulled, I believe, five people from the water.

‌



"One of the girls who works here called emergency services and pinpointed the exact location for them to attend. Between them, they took one of the girls over and banged her on the back until she brought up seaweed, which was quite traumatising for them.

"I'm so proud of them all for coping; it's the first time they've had to deal with something like that.

"Their mums were called to support them, and they then went home. Later, a local paramedic I know asked if we could use the premises for the paramedics and air ambulance crews to debrief. It took an hour and a half, so I left them to it because it's private."

‌



View 4 Images Police speaking to beach hut owners at West Mersea yesterday (Image: Humphrey Nemar/ DAILY MIRROR)

Not the first tragedy at 'dangerous' beach spot

Melissa French, 53, who works at the same café, described the incident as a "tragedy waiting to happen" - and said residents had long called for better signage and life saving equipment along West Mersea Beach.

The drownings on Wednesday night took place not far from where 30-year-old father David Cole drowned in 2023 while saving the life of his three-year-old son.

‌



Mrs French said: "There's a drop on either side, so if you step down, all of a sudden you go from standing on a sandbank to being up to here in water. It's a tragedy waiting to happen.

"If there are two known sandbanks, why are there no warning signs or flags to say 'do not swim in this area'? Because both of those have been where people were on sandbanks or people just don't know the water.

"If you stand on them sandbanks it's softening, once you get off that it's so deep and then you get stuck in the mud you're in trouble. It's like a vacuum, and if you don't know how to get out of it, you're in real trouble.

‌



"If you're in a rip tide you're meant to swim parallel to the shore. But again, there's no signage."

A spokesperson for Colchester Council said "decisions on water safety measures" are "informed by professional risk assessments and advice from specialist organisations".

The statement added: "As part of our risk assessment process for the site, the council commissioned an independent RLSS UK beach risk assessment in March 2026, which did not recommend the installation of public rescue equipment within the assessed area of West Mersea beach.

‌



"The assessment concluded that, due to factors including the beach profile, tidal range and lateral currents, public rescue equipment would be unlikely to be deployed effectively in an emergency and was therefore not recommended on that stretch of coastline.

"We continue to work closely with partner organisations through the Mersea Water Safety Forum, a multi-agency partnership that brings together organisations with expertise and responsibilities in water safety.

"Together, the forum assesses local risks and develops and implements measures to help improve safety in and around the water."

‌



View 4 Images A local man and three teenagers from a local café rushed onto the beach to help (Image: Humphrey Nemar/ DAILY MIRROR)

Mirror's Save Lives for Sam campaign

Tomorrow is World Drowning Prevention Day - and the Mirror is continuing its fight for 'Sam's Law' and mandatory water safety education to stop more families losing their loved ones.

Launched in June after a devastating spike in water-related deaths during the heatwave, the Mirror's Save Lives for Sam campaign is named in honour of Sam Haycock, a 16-year-old boy who tragically drowned at Ulley Reservoir in Rotherham, South Yorkshire, in May 2021.

Article continues below

A total of 29 people drowned in open water in May and June this year alone, and 10 so far in July.

News.title: Man makes new friend at work and then discovers she's his long-lost sister
News.content:
Man makes new friend at work and then discovers she's his long-lost sister

Dave Green, 60, made friends with Andrea Urmston, 53, at work after bonding over a shared interest in motorbikes - and later discovered she was his long-lost sister

View 2 Images Dave Green, 60, discovered Andrea Urmston, 53, was his long-lost sister (Image: BBC/PA Wire)

A man has told how he made a new friend at work - only to discover it was his long-lost sister.

‌



Dave Green, 60, was a bus station supervisor at Manchester Airport when he realised Andrea Urmston, who came into the station regularly to fill up vending machines, was a sibling.

‌



The pair had bonded over an interest in motorbikes and had been friends for two years, before a chat about fostering in 2007 led Mr Green to reveal he had been adopted.

‌



Ms Urmston, 53, told him her brother had been put up adoption - and when they talked through the details, they realised they had the same mother.

View 2 Images The pair met while working at Manchester Airport (file photo)

Couple buy cute house in small town but then realise they aren't alone READ MORE :

Mr Green told the BBC: “People don’t meet like that, it’s not what happens in everyday life, but ours are not everyday lives any more.”

‌



Mr Green went on to meet his biological mother, Susan, who gave birth to him when she was 15 - and found he had driven past her home in Altrincham, Trafford, regularly as a bus driver.

Ms Urmston said the first meeting between her brother and their mother was “amazing”.

She said: “It was just something she had wanted so much and she just couldn’t believe it.

‌



“It was a surreal moment, there was lots of tears and then we all just hugged.

“I couldn’t believe that I’d got my brother and my mum together.”

‌



Mum Susan kept a picture of Dave on the mantlepiece as a baby, which had been sent to her just days after the adoption was finalised.

Growing up, the exact same photograph was proudly displayed in Dave's own house.

Dave learnt he was adopted aged 10 when his parents had shown him the paperwork - but said he enjoyed a very happy childhood, and had never attempted to track down his birth mother.

‌



Susan had later made efforts to find her son with the help of the Salvation Army, but had not turned up any results.

Dave and Andrea have found that despite growing up apart they share similar tastes - including taking their tea the same way, and having a love of “tomato sauce butties”.

Mr Green said: “I have always thought it’s not what you have in your life it’s who you have in your life.

Article continues below

“Somebody or something gave me the thumbs up that day and things will never be the same again, things haven’t been the same for 20 years and they’re not going to be ever again because I’ve got the one thing in my life that I need to make it special.”

News.title: Amy Winehouse's mum shares painful truth of star's addiction on death anniversary
News.content:
Amy Winehouse's mum shares painful truth of star's addiction on death anniversary

On the 15th anniversary of Amy Winehouse's death, the singer's mum has opened up about why she thinks her daughter suffered from alcohol addiction, calling her a 'victim of her own success'

View 5 Images Amy Winehouse in 2007 (Image: Getty Images for NARAS)

Amy Winehouse's mother has said her daughter ended up being the "the victim of her own success" as she marks 15 years since her tragic death.

Back to Black singer Amy died on 23 July, 2011. She was found dead at her home in London with a toxicology report later ruling the death as accidental alcohol poisoning. The 27-year-old had struggled with addiction for years and her blood alcohol level at the time of her death was more than five times the legal drink-driving limit.

15 years on, Janis Winehouse, 72, said that she thought Amy's huge rise to fame ended up being her downfall as she used alcohol to cope with her unusual lifestyle.

View 5 Images Amy with her mum Janis Winehouse (Image: Getty Images)

She told the i Paper : "She didn't want [fame], but it just followed her. And she'd be like 'Who me?' She didn't have confidence. Hence the alcohol. I think it's the same with many, many addicts with alcohol. The alcohol takes away the pain and that is a horrible thing with addiction."

Janis said that addiction becomes the "only boss" and said people "don't get" how it can make your body think you "need it". Amy's mother also shared how she was coping with her daughter's death after over a decade. She said that she was simply trying to "get on with life".

5 View 5 Images Janis Winehouse in 2011 after Amy's death (Image: WireImage) 5 View 5 Images Mitch Winehouse, Amy Winehouse and Janis Winehouse (Image: Getty Images)

Earlier this month, Janis and the rest of Amy's family hosted a tribute event to her at Camden Market, where fans could pay their respects to the late singer.

Amy's friend and bassist Dale Davis, who the singer once described as her "favourite person to go anywhere wit", previously told the Mirror about speaking to her the night before she died. "I spoke to her three hours before she went to bed," he shared.

"She called me at 11:30 at night, and we're having a chat for about 15 minutes, and I said I was going to see her tomorrow and she said, 'Okay'. And I said 'Love you'. She said 'love you' and put the phone down. And that was the last thing I heard."

View 5 Images Amy Winhouse performing for MTV in 2007 (Image: FilmMagic)

He revealed the following day he was working with Will Young when he started to get a "barrage of texts". "I didn't understand what was going on," Dale said. "I was starting to get agitated at that point as I was playing still. The musical director then came over and said, Amy's passed. They'd known for about half an hour, and I just slumped back on my chair and said I was supposed to see her tonight."

Since Amy's death, the Amy Winehouse Foundation set up Amy's Place, a recovery house in East London for women battling drug and alcohol addiction. The charity celebrated its 10th anniversary this year.

If you are struggling with alcohol abuse or addiction, advice and support can be found at alcoholchange.org.uk

News.title: Southport killer Axel Rudakubana appears to be manipulating the system, families' lawyer says
News.content:
A lawyer for the families of the children murdered by Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has said his transfer from prison to a psychiatric hospital may be an attempt to "manipulate the system" and added "being evil does not mean that you're suffering with psychosis".

Rudakubana, 19, was given a life sentence for the murder of three children - Alice da Silva Aguiar, 9, Bebe King, 6, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, 7 - and attempted murder of eight other children and two adults.

On Thursday, he was moved from HMP Belmarsh to Broadmoor psychiatric hospital in Berkshire.

Prisoners who are considered to present a risk to staff, inmates or themselves because of mental disorders can be moved to hospital under the Mental Health Act.

Next Wednesday marks two years since Rudakubana carried out the attack at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class on 29 July 2024.

Lawyer Chris Walker, who represents the three bereaved families, said they "don't believe the merits" of the transfer on the basis of a mental health issue and is calling for more information from ministers.

"In my mind this is a new event, this is something which occurred whilst he was at prison, and we at this stage don't believe the merits of it in terms of him because I've seen no evidence at all until today which suggests he has a significant mental health disorder," Walker told BBC Radio 4's Today Programme.

"We do have an evil person but being evil does not mean that you're suffering with psychosis of some sort.

"We need to know is this a single event, is this a recurring event, is this him playing the system and we need those answers."

The Prison Officers' Association told the BBC that Rudakubana was transferred due to a deterioration in his mental health.

Walker added in a separate statement that the news would "devastate" the families at any time but "the fact that this has occurred as we approach the second anniversary in our view is another move by AR who would appear to be attempting, once again, to manipulate the system".

"We have been given the barest of details and whilst we are supporting the families through this we are urgently seeking a meeting with the appropriate authorities to understand the situation before commenting further."

Prior to Rudakubana's sentencing last year, his defence lawyer told the court no psychiatric evidence could suggest a mental disorder contributed to his actions.

Stan Reiz KC added that his client had appeared to have been a "normal child" until he reached 13.

"However, he did make a transition from a normal, well-disciplined child to someone who was capable of committing acts of such shocking and senseless violence."

Handing down the judgement, Justice Julian Goose said: "Many who have heard the evidence might describe what he did as evil, who could dispute it?"

He added: "I am sure Rudakubana had the settled determination to carry out these offences and had he been able to, he would have killed each and every child - all 26 of them."

The Southport Public Inquiry has heard evidence about his past mental health conditions.

In May 2025 there was an investigation after Rudakubana allegedly attacked a prison officer with boiling water.

Confirming the transfer on Thursday, the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) said the families of those murdered and injured would be in the country's heart forever and "our thoughts remain with them" and said it does not change Rudakubana's sentence.

Rudakubana was given a 52-year prison sentence in January 2025 but the judge was unable to impose a whole life order due to Rudakubana being 17 when he carried out the attack. He will likely never be released.

Under the Mental Health Act, the MoJ is likely to have had no choice but to accept doctors' recommendations about whether Rudakubana could be held safely in prison.

The law requires he be transferred back to prison when he no longer requires treatment in hospital. His sentence is not being converted into a "hospital order", which would mean he stayed at Broadmoor.

News.title: 'Extremely significant' bomb in car intercepted on way to NI, Irish police say
News.content:
A car containing an "extremely significant" bomb has been intercepted in the Republic of Ireland as it was being driven across the border for an attack in Northern Ireland, police have said.

The vehicle was stopped during an operation targeting dissident republican activities on Wednesday. Two people were subsequently arrested.

Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly confirmed on Friday that officers found an explosive device and described it as an "extremely significant seizure".

The vehicle was stopped on the N2 near Carrickmacross, County Monaghan, at about 15:00 local time on Wednesday.

A woman in her 20s, who was the driver of the vehicle, was arrested on Wednesday afternoon and a man in his 40s has since been arrested.

GardaÃ­ (Irish police) requested the assistance of the Irish Defence Forces Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) team who examined the vehicle.

News.title: Angela Rayner rules out rent controls in England
News.content:
Housing Secretary Angela Rayner has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham is not looking at bringing in rent controls in England.

She told BBC Breakfast that changes made through the Renters' Rights Act, which came into effect in May, were "already having a significant impact on the market".

She added that controls which had been implemented in some areas of the UK over the past few years had not "necessarily brought rents down".

In 2023 when he was the mayor of Greater Manchester, Burnham called for freezes to private sector rents until the cost of living crisis was over.

But Rayner told the BBC on Friday: "I don't think that rent freezes, rent controls, is a way forward at the moment.

"Three years ago, Andy called for that because there was a significant crisis in the rental market.

"We implemented between then the Renters' Rights Act which is giving renters more power and control."

Temporary rent controls were introduced in Scotland in October 2022 but expired last year.

Under new legislation, ministers in Holyrood will be able to designate certain places in Scotland as rent control areas - expected to come in by 2027.

Councils will be able to cap rent increases on some properties at a maximum of 6%.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski has said he wants to see rent controls brought in for all rented property in England.

Responding to Rayner's interview, he described Burnham as "continuity Starmer", posting on X: "The new prime minister talks a lot of about helping with the cost of living crisis. This is the one single measure that would help the most and save billions. All talk."

Sir Sadiq Khan, the mayor of London, has long called on the government to implement a cap.

The term rent controls describes a range of measures a government can implement - from capping price increases to freezing them for a period of time.

Landlord groups say they may exacerbate the housing crisis by putting owners off renting out property.

The Renters' Rights Act was brought in to give more stability and security to the 11 million people who rent from private landlords.

Under the legislation, fixed-term tenancies have been banned and it is now significantly harder for landlords to evict tenants.

Rents can also only be increased once a year to the property's "open market rent".

News.title: Fifty women tell BBC they were pressured into having sex with strangers
News.content:
Warning: This story contains details of sexual acts

Fifty women have told the BBC they were pressured or coerced by their partners into having sex with strangers.

They got in contact following an investigation which told the story of a woman who said she had been pressured into having sex with more than 100 people she did not know.

Many of the women who came forward said they had sex through swinging despite not wanting to, either because they feared the consequences of refusing or felt they had to keep their partners happy.

They spoke of deep, long-lasting trauma.

"I remember many nights of my partner keeping me up all night screaming at me, threatening me, and attempting to gaslight me into believing this was something I wanted," said one woman. "It was never what I wanted."

Another told us: "I felt like I had been given away. I felt used. I felt so dirty."

Most encounters were arranged via the website FabSwingers, say the women, which claims to have more than half a million UK active monthly accounts.

Six women told BBC News they had been raped by men met through the site.

One said her partner had forced her to have sex with more than 90 men through FabSwingers. On one occasion, he held her down by the ankles, she told us.

Sixteen said intimate photos of them had been uploaded to the website without their permission.

News.title: Hero swimmer helped two children during West Mersea beach tragedy
News.content:
Witnesses say a heroic day-tripper managed to haul two children back to shore during an incident where a mother and daughter drowned.

Beverly Smit, 60, described the unnamed rescuer swimming out to sea three times as the tragedy unfolded in West Mersea, near Colchester, on Wednesday evening.

Shally Rahman, 41, and Samiha Rahman, 15, were trying to rescue a seven-year-old boy from the water when they got into difficulty and died.

Essex Police said the group, from Barking, east London, were all related to each other and the boy remained in hospital, fighting for his life.

Recalling the moment the "Good Samaritan" sprang into action, Smit said: "They were calling for help and the children and adults were out there.

"He swam out, I think, three times. Two of the children he brought back were not in good condition.

"It's not an easy swim when the tide's coming in - you're swimming against the tide. The water [on Wednesday] was particularly quite cold."

News.title: They became best friends – then discovered they were brother and sister
News.content:
Dave Green and Andrea Urmston found they instantly hit it off when their paths crossed while working in separate roles at Manchester Airport.

The two strangers got on so well they could complete each other's sentences - which made sense when they discovered the truth.

Dave was Andrea's biological brother, but had been adopted by another family when he was a baby.

"I was shaking, I was just shaking and my heart was pounding," Andrea told the BBC. "I'd finally found him. It's unbelievable."

In 2005, Dave was managing the bus station at the airport and Andrea serviced the vending machines.

Over the next two years they became firm friends, texting and phoning each other when they were not at work.

One day during a phone call, Dave told Andrea something he had never mentioned before. He was adopted and his birth name was Stuart Proudlove.

"I kind of froze and didn't speak for a minute," said Andrea.

Her maiden name was Proudlove and she had a brother who was adopted before she was born.

"It's not a very popular name and it had to be him. Other than family, I had never heard that surname anywhere else," she added.

She immediately rang her mother, Susan, to check her long-lost brother's birth date. They matched: 24 March 1966. She called Dave straight back.

"I said 'it's got to be you, it's got to be you', and I said 'I need to see you', and so I went to pick him up," Andrea said.

News.title: Heat health alerts in effect for parts of UK as rain returns for some this weekend
News.content:
Yellow heat health alerts came into effect across central and southern England on Friday morning with temperatures forecast to reach 30C (86F) in places.

The alerts, issued by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), cover the East and West Midlands, eastern England, London, south-east England and south-west England and are valid from 09:00 BST on Friday until 09:00 on Sunday.

The UKHSA warns that heat is expected to cause minor impacts for health and social care services, with an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

It comes as parts of the UK prepare to see much-needed rain this weekend - although amounts are expected to be relatively small, especially in the south.

A drought was officially declared for large parts of north and mid-Wales on Thursday.

The rest of Wales, along with much of central, southern and eastern England, is in "prolonged dry weather" category - one stage below a drought - and the Sottish Environment Protection Agency said much of eastern Scotland has moved into 'water scarcity' status

Hosepipe bans are in force for millions of the customers across eastern and southern England.

News.title: PM to spend first day working from northern branch of No 10
News.content:
Burnham told the assembled civil servants "It's not just a new office - through this place power is going to flow, energy is going to flow."

He added: "It's sending a message to everyone here that we've got support of the government from the very top - it's a very powerful message. The political commitment is there."

Other ministers due for meetings at the Manchester hub on Friday include Angela Rayner, Pat McFadden, Jonathan Reynolds, Yvette Cooper, Angela Eagle, Heidi Alexander and Miatta Fahnbulleh.

Insisting the move would not be short-lived, Burnham said No 10 North was not just for north-west England but for every region and nation of the UK.

"There'll be many voices out there, I can hear them all already, often London based, but not exclusivelyâ¦ They like to say, 'Oh, this will just be the new levelling up, or another sort of short-lived gimmick', and they'll also say 'What's it going to cost?'"

He continued: "What does it cost for everybody to troop down to London every time there's a meeting when you need to make an argument about something?

"What does that cost? So actually, isn't it better that we have a North Pole that balances the South Pole of our country, where power will always be concentrated?

"At least it creates that sense of a more balanced country, and that big things can be done from here."

Burnham will chair a meeting of the National Economic Council, a cabinet committee first launched in 2008 to respond to economic challenges around the UK.

The meeting will bring together senior ministers and regional mayors to "put devolution at the centre of the government's mission to make Britain better".

Strategic decisions about devolution and local economic growth will shift from the Treasury and the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government to No 10 North, although both departments will have input in these areas.

Asked whether Burnham's messaging was too focused on the north of England, Rayner told BBC Breakfast people understood No 10 North was about driving growth in every postcode across the UK.

News.title: Firefighting helicopter brought in to tackle Isle of Wight blaze
News.content:
A helicopter has been brought in as firefighters continue to fight a large heathland blaze on the Isle of Wight.

The gorse fire was first reported at Headon Warren, in the West Wight, shortly after 09:00 BST on Thursday, and is affecting a 25-hectare (62-acre) area of woodland.

Crews from Hampshire and Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service worked overnight to extinguish the blaze using jets and hose reels and have arranged for a helicopter water-drop to reach inaccessible areas.

Additional fire appliances have been taken to the island to support the efforts to fight the fire which is on land owned by the National Trust. The public has been told to stay away.

News.title: Novel analysis reveals playful side of Alan Turing
News.content:
A story written by World War Two codebreaker Alan Turing suggests he was a man with playful humour embracing his homosexuality, according to new analysis.

The six-page hand-written short story, Pryce's Buoy, has been transcribed in full for the first time and studied by Sarah Dillon, professor of literature at the University of Cambridge.

Dillon said the story offered fresh insights that challenge the view of Turing as an isolated, lonely genius.

"We've distilled a version of Turing that is a two-dimensional stereotype," she added.

Turing played a crucial role in the Allies' victory over Nazi Germany in World War Two by helping to crack codes and deciphering the infamous Enigma machine at Bletchley Park.

After the war he produced a detailed design for a digital computer in the modern sense, storing programmes in its memory.

News.title: UK mortgage rates rise to highest level for a month
News.content:
UK average mortgage rates have risen back to the level of a month ago as renewed tensions in the Middle East feed through to homeowners.

Lenders' funding costs have increased as markets judge that a prolonged conflict reduces the possibility of interest rate cuts by central banks.

The five biggest High Street banks are among a host of lenders which have increased their interest rates on new fixed deals in recent days.

Recent projections by the Bank of England suggest just over five million homeowners should expect their monthly mortgage repayments to increase by the end of 2028.

Mortgage rates had been falling as a ceasefire between the US and Iran initially appeared to hold.

But fresh strikes and Houthi militia attacks on oil tankers in the Red Sea reignited fears over global energy supplies.

Oil prices hit $100 a barrel for the first time since May on Thursday after several days of increases, stoking fears of higher inflation and a lower likelihood of interest rate cuts.

News.title: Man who paid for children to be sexually abused jailed
News.content:
A 76-year-old man who paid for children in the Philippines to be sexually abused to order has been jailed.

Robert Pasteiner, from Chichester, West Sussex, was identified through suspicious payments totalling more than Â£200,000 made to individuals in the South East Asian country, including arrested facilitators of live-streamed child sexual abuse.

He was arrested at Heathrow Airport in 2023 before he was due to fly to the Philippines.

Pasteiner was sentenced at Portsmouth Crown Court to 12 years in prison after pleading guilty to 36 offences.

Mobile phone analysis discovered that he had arranged to meet a 12-year-old girl in his hotel in the Philippines.

A search of his luggage found condoms and Viagra, as well as presents.

Further searches of his home uncovered 15 electronic devices, six of which contained indecent images of children.

Paperwork seized contained payment details, how much money had been sent and what the payments were for â noting some as being for a "show".

Pasteiner pleaded guilty to causing or inciting the sexual exploitation of a child, attempted sexual communication with a child, arranging or facilitating the sexual exploitation of a child and making indecent images of children.

He also received a Sexual Harm Prevention Order and will be on the Sex Offender's Register for life.

The National Crime Agency (NCA) said it worked with the National Bureau of Investigation and Philippine National Police to identify and safeguard his victims.

Senior investigating officer Danielle Pownall said: "Robert Pasteiner is a depraved man who posed a significant threat to children around the world.

"The items recovered during our investigation are a clear sign of his intentions in travelling to the Philippines."
