Sports.title: Leandro Paredes drops Lionel Messi retirement bombshell in rapid return to football
Sports.content:
Leandro Paredes has claimed Lionel Messi had already decided the World Cup final would be his final game for Argentina.

Speculation has been rife over Messi's international future after he was unable to inspire his country to World Cup glory, as they were beaten 1-0 by Spain after extra-time in a one-sided final.



5 Lionel Messi is yet to tell the world what the future holds for him on the international stage Credit: Getty

Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th-minute, with the match being marred by ugly scenes afterwards.

A mass brawl broke out when Argentina's players were involved in a series of bust-ups, with midfielder Paredes at the heart of this as he threw punches and grappled with Spain's Eric Garcia and Gavi.

Meanwhile Messi was left heartbroken by the defeat in New York, breaking down in tears after receiving his runners-up medal.



At 39, there is every chance this was the footballing icon's last game for his national team, although he is yet to officially confirm this.

'It hurts'

The fallout from the ill-tempered World Cup final has continued in recent days, with Argentina coming in for huge criticism for their actions at the final whistle, not least Paredes.



FIFA are set to launch an investigation into the ugly full-time scenes, and the 32-year-old could well face punishment for his actions.

But Paredes certainly hasn't put his life on hold as he awaits his fate, making his return to club football with Boca Juniors on Thursday.



In a remarkably quick turnaround, the Argentina star played the full 90 minutes and assisted the only goal as his side claimed a 1-0 win over O'Higgins in the Copa Sudamericana.

After the match, Paredes was asked about Messi's international future, and replied: "It hurts because I think we said it throughout the World Cup - we didn't want his last game to come.

"I think he had already decided that this would be his last game with the national team.

5 Paredes admitted he thinks Messi has already made his mind up on his Argentina future Credit: X: @messixtrahq



5 The midfielder returned to play a key role for Boca Juniors in their Copa Sudamericana last-16 play-off win Credit: Getty

”I hope not - I hope he can keep playing. It’ll be his decision, and whatever he decides, if it makes him happy, it’ll make us happy too. So, let’s hope so.”

As for Paredes, he received a hero's welcome as he took to Boca Juniors' iconic La Bombonera home as captain once again.

The ex-Paris Saint-Germain midfielder has been widely criticised for his violent rampage in the World Cup final, not least from talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor, who called for him to be banned from the next edition of the tournament.



Back on home turf though, Paredes received a warm reception from the fans of his hometown club, and he expressed his appreciation afterwards.

He said: "[I have] nothing but gratitude to the fans.

"Having the fans applaud and cheer for me throughout the entire match is a beautiful thing. I am truly grateful."

5 Paredes was back in action days after his violent rampage in the World Cup final Credit: Getty

Messi retirement: What has been said?

With Paredes sharing his belief that Messi has likely played his final game for Argentina, this isn't the only hint towards his international retirement in recent days.



Moments before the World Cup final, Messi was seen addressing his teammates, where he tells them to 'forget about everything else'.

Footage from the tunnel shows the Argentina captain trying to motivate his players, who all appear downbeat.

He says: "Let's just concentrate on playing, nothing else - calm, okay? Forget everything else."

While it is unclear what exactly the Albiceleste captain was telling his teammates to forget about, there has speculation this could be in response to him announcing his international retirement to them.



This would perhaps explain the emotionally charged performance from the 2022 world champions in the final.

5 Messi was in tears after collecting the second World Cup runners-up medal of his career Credit: Getty

While they were typically aggressive, this boiled over in the latter stages, with Enzo Fernandez being sent off towards the end of normal time.

And their aggression turned into pure chaos at full-time in a mass brawl, as Paredes threw punches, while Nahuel Molina struck Spain captain Rodri.



Messi is yet to address his international future himself, who released an emotional statement in the aftermath of Argentina's final defeat sharing his heartbreak, and thanking fans for their support.

The sporting great scored eight goals and assisted another four at the World Cup - only failing to contribute against Spain.

He hinted at possible retirement before kick-off as his boots for the final had 'El Ultimo Tango', which is 'The Last Tango', written on them.

However, he is under contract at Inter Miami until December 2028, and there is nothing concrete in regards to him calling it quits.

Sports.title: Falkland Islands team address Argentina World Cup banner during Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
Argentina's Falkland Islands banner has been labelled 'disappointing' by a Commonwealth Games athlete.

The World Cup finalists displayed the message as they celebrated their semi-final win over England last week.



3 Argentina's Falklands message has been branded 'disappointing' ahead of the Commonwealth Games Credit: AFP

Players held up a banner reading 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates to 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

The reference to the British Overseas Territory has reignited tensions from the 1982 Falklands War.

Whilst FIFA have since launched a probe into the incident, Falkland Islands athlete Cecil Alexander has now addressed the incident.



The 45-year-old is one of six members of their team at the Commonwealth Games, which began in Glasgow on Thursday.

All six representatives will compete in bowls, with Alexander part of the men's singles draw.



He addressed the incident following his opening match, a straight sets defeat to Malaysia's Izzat Shameer Dzulkeple.

Speaking to the Guardian, Alexander admitted: "It’s disappointing when politics gets mixed with sport.



"We are here to compete and represent our country. We keep politics out of it."

Having moved to the Falkland Islands from South Africa eight years ago, he added: "I am fairly new to the Falkland Islands but I am enjoying (living there)."

The Commonwealth Games began on Thursday with the opening ceremony and will run until Sunday, August 2.

3 Alexander is one of six bowlers representing the Falkland Islands at the Commonwealth Games Credit: Getty



Live coverage from Glasgow will be available on talkSPORT throughout the Games.

Natalie Sawyer presents commentary from Friday evenings' events from 7pm, live on talkSPORT.

Argentina latest

The fallout to Argentina's banner has continued following their post-match antics against the Three Lions.

Several players risked potential bans by holding up the political message in front of their supporters inside the Mercedes-Benz Stadium.



A statement has since been released by a group of Argentine veterans from the 1982 conflict calling for calm.

Meanwhile, the executive director of the White House's World Cup task force defended the Argentina players' right to display the message.

3 FIFA have launched a probe into Argentina's Falklands banner Credit: Getty

Now former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer issued a stern response to the banner, though, reiterating that the Islands are British territory.



Starmer's spokesperson said: "The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are.

"Our position is unchanged. Self-determination rests with the islanders and our commitment to the Falklands will never waver.

"More broadly, potential action is a matter for FIFA, but it’s been a fantastic World Cup and we’ve said throughout that politics should stay out of football."

Sports.title: 23 million people signed petition demanding Argentina’s lifetime ban from the World Cup
Sports.content:
Millions want to see Argentina banned from competing in future World Cups, and now another petition has since been launched as angry fans demand a rematch of the final they lost

An online petition demanding that Argentina's national team be permanently banned from the World Cup gathered more than 23 million signatures in under one week.

The appeal, titled 'Argentina Out,' drew a ridiculous 23,316,108 signatures from 170 countries worldwide.



4 Millions of fans have called for Argentina to be banned from the World Cup for life Credit: Getty

An initial target of five million was set by organisers, but the final total blew past that to become one of the most circulated online petitions in history.

Launched during the 2026 World Cup by irate football fans, it accused FIFA and match referees of 'bias' towards Argentina and captain Lionel Messi, something FIFA strongly denied.

"Why should the rest of the teams play in the tournament if the winner is known in advance?" the text on the petition read.



"Exclude Argentina from the World Cup and give everyone a fair chance."

La Albiceleste were beaten 1-0 in Sunday's final by Spain, and legendary forward Messi left the pitch in tears amid ugly scenes at the full-time whistle.



Following the conclusion of the tournament, in which Argentina's behaviour had been described as 'classless', the petition has been closed.

Its website now reads: "FIFA ignored us but Spain delivered. Thank you Spain."



Ultimately, angry fans haven't got their wish, and Argentina will continue to compete in future World Cup tournaments, starting in 2030, where they are one of multiple hosts for an expanded, 64-team format.

Anti-Argentina petition came close to setting world record

With more than 23 million signatures, the 'Argentina Out' petition fell just short of a Guinness World Record.

The Jubilee 2000, an international movement which called for the cancellation of unpayable debts owed by the world's poorest countries, still holds the record.

It began in April 1997, and by the time it was handed over at the UN Millennium summit in New York at the end of 2000, the number of signatories had reached 24,319,181 from 166 countries.



4 The anti-Argentina petition came close to setting a world record for signatures Credit: Getty

As wide as its circulation was, the 'Argentina Out' petition was never going to have any serious impact on FIFA, or international football as a whole.

The sport's governing body never acknowledged its demands, and any other online movement like it will never have any legal bearing on the nation's participation in international tournaments.

Counter-petition launched to replay World Cup final

That fact, though, hasn't deterred Argentina fans from creating their own petition in the wake of World Cup final heartbreak.



In the days since the showpiece in New York, more than 80,000 fans have reportedly signed an Argentine petition to replay the match due to 'rigged refereeing decisions.'

Gisela Sanchez created the petition page on Change.org, and appealed for fellow supporters to back her call for a rematch.

However, while her petition has gathered more than 80,000 signatures, the organiser has provided no verified evidence to support the allegations.

"The recent final between Argentina and Spain was tarnished by the controversial and corrupt performance of the referee who, according to video evidence, was bought to influence the match’s outcome," she wrote, sharing the baseless claim.



4 A counter petition has called for the World Cup final to be replayed Credit: Getty

4 Some fans in Argentina believe the World Cup was 'rigged' against them Credit: Getty

"It is a MONUMENTAL disappointment for the players, coaches, and, above all, for the fans who crave to see a game decided by talent and dedication on the pitch, and not by rigged refereeing decisions.

"If we allow corruption to go unnoticed on this global stage, we are setting a bad example for future generations of athletes and fans.



"Therefore, we ask FIFA to review these incidents with seriousness and transparency, and to consider replaying the final -- this time without the influence of a CORRUPT referee."

Much like the 23 million strong appeal against Argentina, an online call to replay the final will have no legal or sporting effect on the result, or Spain's second World Cup title.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp comes out of retirement after two years in return to management
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp comes out of retirement after two years in return to management

Jurgen Klopp has officially returned to management, replacing Julian Nagelsmann as Germany boss.

Klopp makes his comeback to the touchline two years after departing Liverpool and suggesting that he had retired.



3 Klopp has now officially replaced Nagelsmann as Germany boss Credit: AFP

He has replaced Nagelsmann as manager of his country after he resigned from his post following World Cup elimination.

Peter Krawietz, Pep Lijnders and Sven Bender have been confirmed as Klopp's assistants.

Germany were knocked out in the last 32 by Paraguay in one of the major shocks of the tournament.



Nagelsmann quit his job earlier this month and that then opened the door for Klopp to come in, amid instant links to the role.

In fact, Germany revealed they had originally opened talks with the former Liverpool manager in Nagelsmann's exit statement.



And those talks have now led to the 59-year-old returning to management and taking the hot seat with his nation.

Klopp said on Friday: "This role is the highlight of my career and I'll give all I've got to be successful."



In an unexpected turn, he also threatened to quit if the media steps over the line during his tenure.

DFB president Bernd Neuendorf added: "We've had very intense discussions. He was our ideal solution from the start.

"And we at the DFB were unanimous in saying he was the candidate we had to talk to.

3 Klopp is back in management two years after leaving Liverpool Credit: AFP



"Our talks with Jurgen only strengthened our belief that he's the right man at the right time."

Back in the dugout

Klopp has not taken a new job since departing Liverpool in 2024, but he's now officially Germany boss.

He became Red Bull's Global Head of Soccer last year, with his contract for that role having a break clause included.

That has allowed him to depart for a return to management.

The legendary ex-Premier League manager replaces Nagelsmann, who took charge of the country in 2023.



Klopp won the top-flight title and the Champions League as Liverpool boss, cementing himself in English football folklore.

3 Klopp is one of the world's most iconic managers and now he's in charge of Germany Credit: AFP

He was on the touchline for 489 games as Reds manager, and now, after two years off, he's made a comeback.

The perfect man for the job

talkSPORT's European football expert, Andy Brassell, believes that Klopp is going to be perfect for the job.



Speaking ahead of his appointment, Brassell said: "This is the perfect time for Klopp... the German FA have had off-the-books talks with him for years.

"He's someone who gets German football culture and someone who can unite the public behind the team.

"You're talking about a guy who's massively popular within the culture and even before he was Dortmund coach."

Former international Robert Huth also told talkSPORT: "I think 99 per cent of Germany would like Klopp in the manager's seat.



"He represents everything they need at the moment - energy, passion, relentlessness."

Sports.title: World Cup player allegedly tests positive for cocaine after being stopped twice by police
Sports.content:
World Cup player allegedly tests positive for cocaine after being stopped twice by police

Australia midfielder Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine after being stopped by police for speeding.

The 22-year-old, who recently competed at the World Cup, was pulled over twice whilst driving in Sydney by officers on Thursday night.

3 Volpato allegedly tested positive for cocaine after being stopped twice by police Credit: Getty

Volpato was stopped in a BMW Coupe on the Anzac Bridge at 11.05pm after he was caught driving between 86kmh and 94kmh in a 60kmh zone, New South Wales police said.

When subjected to a roadside breath test, the Sassuolo star returned a negative result.

Positive test

However, he allegedly tested positive for cocaine when stopped for a second time two hours later.

The latter stop occurred in the same 60kmh zone, with Volpato said to have been travelling at 109kmh at the time.

Police said Volpato was subsequently issued with an infringement notice for driving at excess speed.

His international driver's licence has also been suspended for six months.

This prevents the Socceroos international from driving in the state of New South Wales.

Police inquiries are also set to continue with a secondary sample of oral fluid taken for further analysis.

Australia star

The incident comes just three weeks on from Australia's World Cup exit.

Tony Popovic's side were beaten on penalties in the round of 32 by Egypt on July 3.

3 Volpato's international driving licence has been suspended for travelling at excess speed Credit: Getty

Volpato started the match, one of three appearances he made in North America this summer.

The Camperdown-born starlet was included in Australia's World Cup squad after switching his international allegiance on the eve of the tournament.

He had previously represented Italy at youth level, having qualified for the Azzurri through his grandparents.

Despite turning down a senior Australia call-up in the past, he was included in Popovic's 26-man squad for the World Cup.

Volpato currently has four Socceroos caps to his name following the tournament.

Meanwhile, he has played his club football in Italy since 2020, first joining Roma before a move to Sassuolo three years ago.

3 Volpato made three appearances for Australia at this summer's World Cup Credit: Getty

Australia return to action in September with a pair of friendlies against Brazil in Townsville and Brisbane.

The Socceroos will then turn their attention to the Asian Cup, which will be held in Saudi Arabia in January.

Sports.title: THE ANALYST - Ousmane Diomande, Nottingham Forest's £35m 'coup': Barred from training with Viktor Gyokeres after too many bust-ups, how he muzzled Erling Haaland and why he's the perfect fit for Oliver Glasner and the Premier League
Sports.content:
THE ANALYST - Ousmane Diomande, Nottingham Forest's £35m 'coup': Barred from training with Viktor Gyokeres after too many bust-ups, how he muzzled Erling Haaland and why he's the perfect fit for Oliver Glasner and the Premier League

Read THE ANALYST only on DailyMail+ to get the ultimate lowdown on the world's biggest talents - and tell you how they would fit in at YOUR club

Such is Ousmane Diomande's competitive nature that former Sporting Lisbon manager Ruben Amorim was frequently forced to intervene to stop him and Viktor Gyokeres coming to blows.

So much so, the pair were eventually prevented from playing against each other in training because the threat of a crunching challenge or tensions flaring up was too high. Diomande and the now Arsenal striker had several rows and physical battles on the training pitch. Small-sided games, in particular, became too risky. With the Ivorian centre back set to join Nottingham Forest in a deal worth around £35million, he will get another crack at his former team-mate.

Their rivalry was not born from animosity, rather a perfectionist drive – training, competitive matches or even a kick about in the garden were all treated the same.

That hyper-competitive spirit should see Diomande settle into life at Forest and the Premier League well and impress new manager Oliver Glasner – who once, speaking in a Crystal Palace press conference, admitted that winning is paramount, regardless of whether he was playing with his children or in a major final. They are cut from the same cloth.

Glasner had chased Diomande’s signature at Palace, targeting him as Marc Guehi’s replacement in January. But Palace did not move quickly enough and Diomande signed a new contract until 2030, featuring a prohibitive £68.5m release clause. But now, in his new job, the Austrian has got his man.

The fee represents exceptional value for Forest as they pivot to a back three having played a back four last season. They are getting a player familiar with Glasner's preferred 3-4-2-1, having enjoyed success in that shape under Amorim at Sporting.

Nottingham Forest are understood to be offering £32million for Ivory Coast centre back Ousmane Diomande

Diomande (left) and Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres (centre) were not even allowed to play against each other in training at Sporting Lisbon, such was the ferocity of their rivalry

The 22-year-old joined Sporting Lisbon three years ago from Danish side Midtjylland

Diomande has all the attributes of a defender capable of thriving in the Premier League. Not only is he fast and proficient on the ball but he thrives defensively thanks to his physical strength and solid 6ft 3in build.

In last season’s Champions League, he won 66 per cent of his duels and is a relentless battler. He does not make it easy for attackers. Erling Haaland learned the hard way in a Champions League group stage match two seasons ago, after Diomande marshalled him well throughout as Sporting thrashed Manchester City 4-1 in Lisbon.

His sprint speed will also be a valuable asset. Diomande possesses explosive recovery pace which will help Forest when defending with a high line. His ability to recover quickly will allow Forest to react more effectively when opponents look to exploit the space in behind during transitions. Glasner's Palace side often relied on it with Maxence Lacroix; Forest are likely to be no different with Diomande.

He will feature on the right of Forest’s back three, partnering Murillo and Nikola Milenkovic, as an imposing centre back. In Glasner’s system, he will be given some license to carry the ball forward and play line-breaking passes – which he has the skill set to do.

But at 22 years old, he does lack a bit of wisdom and has been guilty of running himself into trouble with overconfidence in possession. He will need to learn to pick the right moments to carry the ball, but that should come with experience – especially under the guidance of a top-quality coach.

Those who have followed Diomande closely during his time at Sporting told Daily Mail Sport that while the Ivorian exhibits a relaxed aura on the pitch, it has sometimes worked to his detriment – suffering blips in concentration.

That said, he does have know-how beyond his 22 years – making 87 appearances in the Portuguese top flight, 18 in the Champions League, 12 in the Europa League and earning 16 international caps including one at this summer's World Cup. He has silverware to show for it, too, winning the Portuguese top flight twice and the Portuguese Cup.

That was the precise reason he opted to join Sporting. The Portuguese outfit identified him while on loan at second-tier side Mafra from Denmark’s Midtjylland. Despite losing against Porto 3-0 in the cup, Diomande delivered a standout performance, drawing attention from the Sporting scouts. They passed a report to then-head coach Amorim, who immediately wanted to sign him.

He has significant Champions League experience with Sporting, as well as 16 caps for his country

‘We have to give credit to the people who discovered him,’ Amorim later said. ‘The scouting department showed me the player, and once I saw the details, it was immediately clear he was the one, whether he cost €500,000, €2m or €8m.

'He had all the characteristics - the way he played with the ball, his speed. And then there were other details, like going to the Dragao with Mafra and looking as if he was out in the playground. We knew what was there.’

When the January 2023 window opened, Sporting did exactly that, signing him in a £14m deal which will also see them pocket 10 per cent of the profit on this move, around £2.1m. Diomande credits Amorim with his career development and later revealed that the moment he was aware of Amorim’s interest, he wanted to make the move because of his faith in young players.

In Portugal, it was widely accepted that Diomande would eventually depart for one of Europe’s top five leagues. There was a slight surprise, however, that he did not wait for an even bigger move, as they believe he is destined for Europe’s elite. For Forest, that is a wonderful coup – especially if he follows his expected trajectory, which could see his value double in 2-3 years. There is also belief that once the mistakes are ironed out, he has the characteristics to be a leader.

Diomande suits Glasner, will have resale value if a bigger club does come calling and already demonstrated signs of becoming a supreme centre back - it is no wonder Forest want to make him the first marquee signing of the Glasner era. And, for the record, Gyokeres and Arsenal come to the City Ground on October 17. Get the fireworks ready.

Sports.title: Aston Villa in talks to sign another Chelsea outcast after Alejandro Garnacho - as Maxence Lacroix undergoes Blues medical ahead of £55m move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Lacroix closes in on £55m Chelsea move

Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today after the Blues agreed a deal for the Crystal Palace defender worth around £55m on Thursday.

As Daily Mail Sport reported earlier this week, talks accelerated over a meeting in New York at the weekend.

Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali and Palace chairman Steve Parish, who were in New York for the World Cup final, met at the Aman Hotel near Central Park on Sunday.

Daily Mail Sport revealed Chelsea had revisited their interest in the 26-year-old early this summer.

The France international cost Palace £18m from Wolfsburg but has been an outstanding performer in the Premier League and Europe.

Crystal Palace and France star Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today

Villa in talks to sign Jackson

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson.

The clubs have already agreed a loan with obligation deal for Alejandro Garnacho to join Villa. That followed the £117m sale of Morgan Rogers.

The structure of the deals are key as Chelsea and Villa are among those that need to comply with Uefa's squad cost ratio regulations and their 2025 settlement agreements.

Rogers' £117m move will provide Villa with a significant accounting profit, potentially over £80m after Middlesbrough's sell-on clause and the remaining book value of his 2024 signing are deducted.

But if Chelsea had sold Garnacho to Villa as part of the same transaction, Uefa would treat it as a swap deal, impinging on profit margin. Even if Garnacho left on deadline day September 1, that is fewer than the guideline of 45 days, making it harder to argue they are not connected.

A loan with an obligation to buy could still be regarded as part of a swap deal because the 'purchase' has been agreed within 45 days of Rogers' transfer but the conditions give Villa control of when that deal is completed and potential room for manoeuvre with Uefa regulators.

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson

Summerville's Saudi switch confirmed

Al-Hilal have confirmed the signing of winger Crysencio Summerville from West Ham in a deal worth up to £60million.

The 24-year-old, who also had an offer from Roma, had a medical in Amsterdam on Tuesday.

Al Hilal will pay an initial fee of £55m, plus £5m in potential add-ons.

Magpies get their man

Aladji Bamba will wear the number eight shirt vacated by Sandro Tonali, after completing his £30million move to Newcastle United.

Bamba arrived from Monaco on Thursday and Newcastle will pay a further £5.5m in add-ons.

The 20-year-old has signed a five-year contract and manager Eddie Howe said: 'He's another exciting, young signing who we're really looking forward to working with.

'Aladji adds depth and a range of qualities to our midfield options, with a huge potential for growth.

'His development since breaking through at Monaco has been really impressive and something we believe we can help him build on.

'He operates in a deeper role but has the ability to contribute all over the pitch, which he demonstrated in both Ligue Un and the Champions League last season.'

Meanwhile, Newcastle say they have still to receive a formal offer from Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes.

No Blues interest in Bruno

Chelsea are not expected to pursue a move for Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

There had been suggestions that the West London club were interested in the Brazilian international, but Chelsea sources categorically refute this.

Daily Mail Sport understands that Chelsea have not, at any point, enquired about Guimaraes and sources maintain they have no plans to.

BOBBY MANZI

Boro target World Cup star

Middlesbrough are in talks to sign USA midfielder Sebastian Berhalter from Vancouver Whitecaps.

Boro are paying £900,000 for the 25-year-old who has 18 caps and played in all of the USA's World Cup games.

The deal includes a further £600,000 in add-ons.

Berhalter was born in London where his father Gregg, a former USA coach, was a player at Crystal Palace.

Boro remain in talks for left-back Max Arfsten from Columbus Crew also.

Middlesbrough are in talks to sign USA star Sebastian Berhalter from Vancouver Whitecaps

Sports.title: Revealed: Jude Bellingham's brutal dig at World Cup referee as unseen footage goes viral - moments before England star slapped Argentina rival following semi-final defeat
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham furiously hit out at 'shocking' refereeing decisions after England's World Cup semi-final heartbreak against Argentina, footage has revealed.

The Real Madrid star made a point of confronting Ismail Elfath – Lionel Messi's favourite referee – to share his grievances after England's 2-1 loss last week.

Argentina employed roughhouse tactics against England, committing 15 fouls, to book their place in the final against Spain, where they lost 1-0.

Leandro Paredes and Enzo Fernandez were seen as particularly dirty in the opening exchanges of the match.

Both teams came into the match with a heightened sense of rivalry after the South American side's declarations throughout the tournament that the Falkland Islands belong to Argentina.

Fresh footage from the referee's camera has been released by FIFA and in it, Bellingham is seen saying to the referee: 'Some shocking ones there, but all the best.'

Jude Bellingham furiously hit out at 'shocking' refereeing decisions after England's World Cup semi-final heartbreak against Argentina, footage has revealed

He was annoyed at decisions that had gone in Argentina's favour in their tense encounter

Bellingham, who scored seven goals for the Three Lions at the tournament, later slapped Argentina rival Valentin Barco on the back of the head as scenes turned ugly in Atlanta.

In the build-up to the flashpoint, Spurs captain and Argentina defender Cristian Romero was seen goading Bellingham when the final whistle was blown.

He went over to Barco and slapped him on the back of the head.

The full-back then turned around and pushed Bellingham with tempers flaring. Nicolas Otamendi also came over and gave the England man a shove.

Several Argentine players attempted to act as peacemakers, but it looked as if Bellingham and Otamendi wanted more head-to-head action – even when they were separated.

During the celebrations Argentina's stars held aloft a banner that read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates to 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

Despite FIFA's ban on political flags, Romero, Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez and ex-Spurs midfielder Giovani Lo Celso celebrated with the controversial sign after the final whistle.

Captain and star player Lionel Messi was also seen dancing alongside the banner.

Bellingham was goaded by Argentina star Cristian Romero at the final whistle

The midfielder also clashed with Argentina substitute Valentin Barco after the semi-final

Bellingham appeared to slap new Chelsea man Barco on the back of the head

He was also at loggerheads with defender Nicolas Otamendi as other players tried to stop them

FIFA are already looking into disciplinary action relating to the banner and Argentina's behaviour following their loss to Spain in the final.

The South American side's dirty tactics against England, plus the consistent allegations throughout the tournament that things were 'rigged' in their favour, have not done Messi's popularity any favours on these shores.

Messi is now viewed unfavourably among almost half of the participants surveyed by YouGov.

After losing 1-0 to Spain some of the Argentina squad started fights with the Spanish players. Fernandez was sent off in normal time and Paredes was lambasted for attacking Eric Garcia and Gavi after the match.

Even Messi was dragged into their pathetic antics in the final, attempting to get Marc Cucurella sent off for briefly putting his hand over his mouth.

Messi also clashed with Bellingham in the semi-finals, though England fans have to admit that the legend was brilliant towards the end of the match, setting up both of his country's goals.

All of this has had a deleterious effect on Messi's popularity.

Coming into the World Cup, he was viewed favourably by 55 per cent of the public and unfavourably by just nine per cent.

Now, he is seen favourably by only 29 per cent and unfavourably by 44 per cent.

That means that, according to YouGov's poll, Messi's net favourability rating among Britons has fallen from +46 to -15. In short, people don't like him very much.

His score is far worse than his arch-rival Cristiano Ronaldo, whose net rating is -2.

And he certainly lost his stock with Daily Mail Sport's veteran columnist Jeff Powell, who bunged Messi out of his top five all-time players for his antics.

Sports.title: The crack coaching team Andoni Iraola has brought in to bring Liverpool back to the top: A 'fiery' fitness specialist to fight injuries, the solution to set-piece woes and Napoli's title-winning goalkeeping guru
Sports.content:
Liverpool fans are already growing used to the sight of Andoni Iraola as their new head coach but when he takes charge of his first match on Saturday in a friendly against Sunderland in Nashville, he will be flanked by several unfamiliar faces. From a fitness coach that has been with him since way back, two former defenders with nearly 800 Football League appearances between them and a former Napoli goalkeeping guru, this is the team behind the Basque, who has been charged with taking Liverpool back to the top. The first place to start is with right-hand man and Liverpool fan Tommy Elphick, who follows Iraola from Bournemouth alongside Shaun Cooper and Pablo de la Torre. Scrolling back through the archives revealed an article from the Brighton Argus in 2011 when a young Elphick, then playing for the Seagulls in the Championship, said his ultimate dream was a trip to Anfield. Fifteen years on, he is finally there. Elphick takes his lessons in leadership from another former Bournemouth boss, Eddie Howe, who he played under as captain of the Cherries. The 38-year-old is rated so highly that Championship clubs Bristol City and Burnley both reportedly made moves this summer to take him on as head coach. Elphick was a boisterous voice back in the day in a playing career that also saw him play for Aston Villa and Huddersfield – and sometimes was unclear what certain managers were asking of him. But the clarity of Howe’s messaging inspired Elphick to go into coaching when he was forced to retire at just 33 following his 10th operation. Elphick was working as Under 21s manager at Bournemouth when his big break came in 2022-23. Gary O’Neil was promoted to head coach and Elphick was invited to form part of his backroom staff. ‘We went in, took the handbrake off and went for it,’ he said in 2023. Andoni Iraola with Shaun Cooper (centre) and Tommy Elphick (right) in the Bournemouth dugout Iraola has brought three of his Bournemouth colleagues with him to Anfield, where he is expected to bring Liverpool back to the top

Your browser does not support iframes.

When O’Neil was sacked despite keeping the Cherries up, Elphick knew that most of the squad felt disillusioned and that the decision was harsh. This was when the now 38-year-old earned his corn and sources say he was crucial in getting everybody back on board. The new man, Iraola, had wanted to bring over his Rayo Vallecano No 2 Inigo Perez but it was not allowed due to a work permit issue. Perez has since taken the top job at Rayo and led them to the Europa Conference League final last season, earning him a move to Villarreal this summer. Iraola likes to manage from a distance so Elphick and Cooper had a responsibility to take training sessions and to get to know players on a deeper level to help psychologically. When Bournemouth won none of their first nine games to start Iraola’s tenure, the coaches remained calm. On a matchday, Iraola likes to sit in between Elphick and Cooper so he can get a constant dialogue. When the head coach’s voice runs out, he nudges one of the pair to bring some energy on the touchline. Cooper is a set-piece specialist. It is understood the former Bournemouth, Sutton United and Portsmouth defender, born on the Isle of Wight, will focus on offensive, creative set plays while Elphick will take charge of defensive routines. Set-pieces are a problem area for Liverpool, who conceded 23 goals from them last season, behind only Leeds, Crystal Palace and... Bournemouth. In late December, set-piece guru Aaron Briggs paid for it with his job, while set-piece analyst Lewis Mahoney stepped up and has earned plaudits for his work. ‘Shaun is coming up with loads of different set-pieces, he has new ones for us to try each game,’ said Bournemouth midfielder Ryan Christie. Last term, they scored 20 goals from set-pieces, ranking sixth, but at the other end had a problem, conceding the most in the division. ‘I was very lucky with Tommy and Shaun when I arrived at Bournemouth,’ said Iraola when asked on this topic this week in Chicago. ‘They were very prepared, they were very helpful for me in terms of understanding the English culture, the mentality of the players, what they were used to, what they like in training, even the small details that maybe in Spain are different. Elphick was forced to retire at just 33 due to injuries, after a playing career best known for his time playing under Eddie Howe at Bournemouth Cooper (black trainers, centre right) will be tasked with being more hands-on than Iraola with the players ‘Also the experience Tommy has at Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brighton, Huddersfield, they can be in a closer position to the players, they can feel more identified. I am a little bit older. Some of the players maybe didn't know I was a player! ‘So they are very good to me, they are very good coaches, we kind of understand the game similarly and they have different roles in the coaching staff, they help with set-pieces also. That’s the reason I continued with them.’ Another important member of the new backroom team is De la Torre, a fitness coach who has been with Iraola since their time at AEK Larnaca in Cyprus. ‘Pablo is a physical coach but has been with me almost all the years I have been coaching,’ explained Iraola. ‘So for me, he is much more than a physical coach, really. He is an assistant and we know each other very well.’ He has been described as a ‘fiery character’ by local reports and De la Torre will have a big role this season as Iraola, for the first time, must get used to the constant demands of European football and competing on four fronts. Injuries were also a big problem last term. De la Torre told Diario AS in Spain last month: ‘Seeing that daily evolution, football‑wise and human‑wise, is one of the proudest achievements of my career. ‘The key is building a game model and team identity where players truly believe in the coach’s idea. Beyond results, I’m proud to have been part of a group that never stopped believing, competing, and improving. ‘Andoni is incredibly intelligent, leads by example, and has a rare emotional stability in such a visceral sport. From day one, you sense he’s different — his ability to read the game and its needs is almost unique.’ Liverpool conceded 23 goals from set-pieces last season, including Amine Adli's last-minute winner for Bournemouth in January Fitness coach Pablo de la Torre (left) has been with Iraola since their time at AEK Larnaca in Cyprus Iraola will also have Luiz Fernando Iubel by his side. The Brazil-German dual citizen works across loans, Under 21s and Under 18s training groups and acts as a bit of a link man between all groups, which makes him important in pre-season especially for a joined-up pathway. Iubel was formerly assistant manager at Brazilian top-flight side Atletico Mineiro and joined midway through last season. He has supported Liverpool since being awestruck by their feats in the 2005 Champions League final. His role is similar to that of Vitor Matos, one of Jurgen Klopp’s trusted backroom allies, who described it as ‘taking care of players that are between the first and second team’ and finding a pathway for them. Matos is now at Swansea. Completing the backroom setup at Liverpool is new goalkeeper coach Alejandro Rosalen, who won two Serie A titles at Napoli. He replaces Xavi Valero, who lasted just one year in his second stint in the post. Tom Webber joins as the first-team tactical analyst having replaced Roddy van der Ham. Webber went to the University of Birmingham and wrote a paper on the relative age effect in football – how people born after a certain cut-off, such as a school year or sports season starting, get physical and developmental advantages.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp confirmed as Germany manager - and reveals he will QUIT the job 'if you don't leave my family in peace' after World Cup flops' WAGs were criticised following disastrous tournament
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp has been unveiled as Germany manager – and has already revealed what will make him quit the job.

The Liverpool legend, 59, is back in the dugout having enjoyed a stint overseeing Red Bull's football operation after leaving Anfield in 2024, and has been tasked with turning the national team around after another disappointing major tournament.

Julian Nagelsmann was given his marching orders after the Germans crashed out to Paraguay in the Round of 32, leading to an inquest into the team's performance –where the players' WAGs and families were placed under the spotlight.

Nagelsmann's partner also made headlines, with German media reporting that his girlfriend, Lena Wurzenberger, was an almost constant presence in the camp.

But Klopp has already set his stall in a robust unveiling, insisting that he will quit the job immediately if his family face any scrutiny.

'The day you don't want me anymore, you say so and I'm gone, without severance pay,' he said via Bild.

'If you say tomorrow that he's rubbish, I'm gone. Not just one person, it would have to be more than that. If the DFB says he's rubbish, I'm gone. If you behave badly and don't leave my family in peace, I'm gone.'

Jurgen Klopp is Germany's new manager, but has already set out what will make him quit

Klopp says he will leave if the media 'don't leave my family in peace' after his predecessor Julian Nagelsmann's relationship with an ex-reporter made headlines

Klopp also described his appointment to the national team position as 'the highlight of my career'.

'Criticise me if something doesn't work. I'm happy to work on it. It's all about the job. Jurgen Klopp doesn't have a career after the national team. Ideally, this is the highlight of my career.'

Wurzenberger, 34, reportedly caused 'quite a stir' among the squad after being 'more present than probably any national team's coach before her'.

She was first spotted at Germany's pre-tournament camp in Frankfurt, when she was pictured watching training from a balcony along with a host of the players' partners.

And after her boyfriend's side thumped Curacao 7-1 - Wurzenberger hung around to watch the German substitutes complete their warm down.

It was then reported that she accompanied Nagelsmann back to the team hotel, before the duo were seen cycling to training together the following morning.

'There is naturally always that feeling that when the boss's wife is in the room, you might not always be completely honest at the table when talking about the national coach,' local reporters speculated during the tournament.

Klopp met second wife Ulla Sandrock in 2005 and married her that same year

Wurzenberger, and indeed Nagelsmann, also incited criticism from Germany legend Lothar Matthaus, who admitted her constant presence is far from 'ideal'.

The midfielder, who earned 150 caps, said on German television: 'She just shouldn't appear in the pictures too often - that wouldn't be ideal in my opinion.

'The players have days off and their families can come to the hotel. Lena (Wurzenberger) did that too. From my perspective, I think it's perfectly normal.

'Lena was able to come to the hotel just like the players' girlfriends and wives. You can see the solidarity - but the rule shouldn't apply to the coach. It has to happen during the time when we players are seeing their families.'

Nagelsmann and Wurzenberger are reported to have started dating soon after he split from his ex-wife Verena, following 15 years together, in 2022.

At that point Nagelsmann was manager of German giants Bayern Munich - and his new love interest reported on the club for Bild.

An article from the publication announcing their romance read: 'Julian Nagelsmann loves Bild reporter'.

Klopp married social worker and children's writer Ulla Sandrock in December 2005, having met at a pub during an Oktoberfest celebration that same year. He was previously married to ex-wife Sabine, with whom he shares a child.

Elsewhere, Arsenal legend Per Mertesacker will play an integral role in Klopp's transformation of the German national team, having been appointed the new Managing Director of Sport for the federation.

Sports.title: Donald Trump's Folarin Balogun red card intervention scandal takes fresh twist as match-fixing watchdog reveals betting line opened just moments after US striker was sent off at the World Cup
Sports.content:
A gambling watchdog group has flagged the United States' Round-of-16 loss to Belgium as one of seven World Cup matches that may have drawn irregular betting activity during the tournament.

Specifically, the independent Group of Copenhagen cited a predictions market line titled 'Will Folarin Balogun play against Belgium?' as one potential issue, sources told The Athletic.

That line opened on July 2 shortly after Balogun was given a controversial red card in Team USA's Round-of-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. On July 5, after President Donald Trump urged FIFA to rescind Balogun's red card, the governing body opted instead to suspend his one-game ban until after the tournament, thereby allowing him to play in the loss to Belgium.

Curiously, the Group of Copenhagen's report specified that no other similar markets opened for the 14 other players who got a red card during the tournament, according to The Athletic. Now the group has requested an official explanation from FIFA on the Balogun case.

The Daily Mail has sought comment from both FIFA and Polymarket, neither of which have been accused of any misconduct in this case.

Operating under the Council of Europe's Macolin Convention of 2014, the Group of Copenhagen is an independent network that detects and prevents the manipulation of sports competitions around the world. For the 2026 World Cup, the organization reviewed all 104 matches from the tournament, which attracted more than $240 billion bets worldwide, according to the Group of Copenhagen.

A gambling watchdog has opened an investigation into Balogun's red card overhaul

Folarin Balogun (20) fouls Bosnia's Tarik Muharemovic (4), resulting in a red card

Balogun was given a controversial red card in Team USA's Round-of-32 win over Bosnia

Although its full report has not yet been published, a summary of its conclusions has been shared by the Council of Europe.

The US loss to Belgium was among seven 'yellow notices' raised by the Group of Copenhagen, which has two higher levels of concern: orange and red.

'The Group of Copenhagen's notices can be explained by atypical behaviors such as changes in odds or hedging liquidities, there are many explanations that are not manipulations,' Christian Kalb, a gambling industry expert who previously worked with the Group of Copenhagen, told The Athletic.

'The major problem is when there may be a conflict of interest and potential inside information on those issues,' she continued. 'When we speak of prediction markets, we can detect some unusual behaviors but we must be very careful as they can be used for hedging markets.

The Norwegian FA is planning to complain to FIFA over the Folarin Balogun World Cup saga

Meanwhile, the Norwegian FA plans to launch a formal complaint to FIFA over Trump's interference in Balogun's red card ban.

Despite Trump's interventions, the US were thrashed 4-1 by Belgium, yet the 80-year-old has repeatedly boasted about his involvement, adding that FIFA President Gianni Infantino made a 'great decision.'

The antics of Trump and FIFA were widely condemned across the sport, and Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) President Lise Klaveness now says she is planning to formally complain to the governing body's ethics committee.

'When you bend a rule like this, you're on a slippery slope that will put the whole game at risk,' she said. 'It is a worry for the game when you compromise fundamental rules of the game.

'First of all, it should not have happened. It is very important now to have honest communication around it. We all know that this verdict was influenced from external forces and did not have the proper process.

'If you start to adapt in such a way towards state leaders and state politics, you will move your behavior and the organization's behavior, and also the red line of what states' leaders should interfere with. And that happened.'

Defending his role in the saga, Infantino insisted it was an independent decision taken by FIFA's disciplinary committee.

He said: 'They operate autonomously, apply the FIFA's disciplinary code, and decide cases based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts before them.

'Their independence is essential to the credibility and integrity of football, and this must always be respected.'

Defiant Argentina president claims 'people are JEALOUS' that they are 'good at almost everything' as he claps back at criticism of Lionel Messi and Co's shameful World Cup campaign

Argentina's president Javier Milei has declared that people are 'jealous' of his country because they are 'good at almost everything' - despite their shameful antics following their World Cup final defeat.

The libertarian leader, who claimed in April that the Falklands 'will always be Argentine', watched the final from home out of superstition, only to see them lose.

But Milei was left red-faced on Monday after he accidentally published a scheduled tweet celebrating an Argentina victory and announcing a national holiday which the public will now not get.

The president said: 'The problem with Argentina is that we are flashy, we don't go unnoticed, people are jealous of us, and we are good at almost everything.

'I'm sorry, but someone had to say it.'

Milei has been outspoken in the wake of Argentina's 1-0 defeat by Spain and insisted that refereeing decisions went against them. The South Americans had two shots all game.

Argentina president Javier Milei has declared that people are 'jealous' of his country after their World Cup final defeat

Argentina's loss to Spain in the World Cup final was marred by violence and bad behaviour

That flies in the face of the consensus opinion throughout the tournament, which was that Argentina benefited from numerous favourable calls from officials.

He told LN+: 'The match was extremely difficult for us on Sunday, and yet Argentina could have grabbed an equaliser in the final minutes, even though the run of play was not at all favourable to Argentina.

'Argentina always took up stances and behaved in a measured manner throughout the tournament, even in the moments when the referee took incorrect positions towards the Argentina national team in some matches, as they responded in a very measured and organised way, and they were always distinguished fighting until the end.'

Measured and distinguished is one way of putting it for a side who are under investigation by FIFA for their conduct after the final whistle.

Midfielder Leandro Paredes grabbed Spain's Eric Garcia by the neck and pushed over Gavi in ugly post-match scenes.

Meanwhile, Nicolas Otamendi, who has now retired from international football, got into a row with Spain captain Rodri.

Anyone who was relying on Milei for news of the final would have been misled on Monday morning when his scheduled tweet came out.

The embattled president wrote on X: 'WORLD CELEBRATION: Given the concern about the celebrations for the achievement reached by the Argentine National Team, I inform the population that, depending on what the Players and the Technical Staff decide regarding the day to celebrate, it will be declared a national holiday.'

Argentina were unable to repeat their glory of 2022, when they beat France on penalties to win the World Cup, but they should be commended for reaching three finals in the last four editions.

That said, many supporters around the world and several of their opponents felt that the tournament was 'rigged' in Argentina's favour by FIFA.

Milei's popularity has plummeted this year amid corruption allegations, with his cabinet chief recently resigning.

He took up the presidency in 2023.

Sports.title: Argentina star who PUNCHED Spain rival in shameful World Cup final antics hints at quitting international football after 'painful' defeat - but finally admits new world champions 'were the better team'
Sports.content:
Argentina's chief aggressor from the World Cup final, Leandro Paredes, is considering quitting international football.

The midfielder, who grabbed Spain's Eric Garcia by the neck and pushed over Gavi after full time, says the 'pain' of losing will remain with him for a long time.

Paredes was heavily scrutinised for his outburst, during which he appeared to throw punches, and he was fortunate not to be sent off towards the end of normal time for a foul.

It comes as Argentina seem to be headed for a rebuild. Manager Lionel Scaloni was in tears as he hinted at his exit, while Nicolas Otamendi has already announced his retirement. Whether Lionel Messi continues remains to be seen – he is now 39.

Paredes, 32, told ESPN: 'For many, it will be the time to decide if to continue. It was a great journey. Maintaining that level – getting the group to continue to function as it has - will be very difficult, and there are many factors to consider.

'Decisions must be taken calmly. I don't know yet if I'm ready to continue. It's a process that takes time to assimilate and mature.

Argentina's chief aggressor from the World Cup final, Leandro Paredes, could quit international football

The midfielder, who lashed out at Spain's stars at full time, says the 'pain' of defeat will linger

'It will take time to digest what we've been through. The pain of losing the World Cup final will stay with us for a long time, because we came so close once again. I think we played in a World Cup where people saw themselves in us, and that's very rewarding. In that sense, I'm happy.'

FIFA have launched an investigation into the behaviour of the Argentina squad, who turned their backs on Spain during the trophy celebration after losing 1-0 to a Ferran Torres goal.

Spain star Gavi has since insisted that Paredes should not be suspended, but the Argentine was panned by BBC Sport's pundits.

Micah Richards said: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time. Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest.

'Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Fellow BBC pundit Joe Hart added: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Wayne Rooney also gave his views and said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Argentina's players could also face further disciplinary action after FIFA opened an investigation following their semi-final win over England when several of them lifted a controversial banner touting their country’s claim to the Falkland Islands, which read: 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas'.

Argentina star Nicolas Otamendi has retired - after losing the World Cup final and clashing with Rodri

At least Paredes has put the final behind him in some way - he was back playing for Boca Juniors in the Copa Sudamericana this week.

Meanwhile, Otamendi has already walked away from international football.

The former Manchester City star and 2022 World Cup winner has said he is retiring from Argentina with his 'head held high' and with 'peace of mind'.

That's despite the 38-year-old's final act on the global stage being an angry row with Rodri, in which he branded the Spain captain an 'idiot' and accused the victors of whining too much.

The centre-back came on as a substitute on Sunday and was highly involved in Argentina's rearguard action. Spain's first goal by Nico Williams was ruled out because of the controversial call that Mikel Merino had fouled Otamendi.

He steps away after 139 caps – the fifth-most ever for Argentina – and eight goals. Having made his debut for them in 2009, he also went on to lift two Copa Americas.

Otamendi wrote on Instagram: 'Today I have to write the most difficult words of my entire career.

'From a very young age, I dreamed of wearing the Argentine national team jersey; it was the greatest privilege football has given me. I defended it with my soul, with pride, and with the responsibility of knowing what it means to millions of Argentinians.

Otamendi won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina and earned 139 caps for them, the fifth-most in the team's history

'Fate decreed that my last match would be a World Cup final. It wasn't the result we wanted, but I leave with my head held high, knowing that this group tried until the very last second.

'I say goodbye with the peace of mind of having given everything. I never held back an ounce of effort, I never stopped believing, and I never stopped feeling this jersey as the greatest honor of my life.

'Thank you to the Argentine fans. Thank you for your unconditional love, for every flag, for every song, for being with us in the good times and, above all, in the most difficult. You made us feel, every time the anthem played, that we weren't just eleven players, but millions defending the same dream.

'Thank you to my family. They were my refuge in every fall and my strength in every challenge. They endured the distances, the absences, the tears, and the frustrations. I never walked this path alone; we took every step together.

'And to those who still wear this jersey today, I want to say something from the bottom of my heart: never stop believing. There will be blows that seem impossible to overcome, but this jersey always rewards those who defend it with humility, sacrifice, and love. Hold your heads high, keep fighting, and don't let a defeat steal your hope. I am convinced that the next chapter of our story will be yours.

'Today I say goodbye to the Argentine national team, but with immense pride for having represented my country. Because titles remain in history, but the love for these colors lasts a lifetime.

'Thank you, Argentina. Thank you for letting me fulfil the dream of being a world champion and wearing the most beautiful jersey in the world.'

Otamendi has said he is walking away with his 'head held high' and with 'peace of mind'

Otamendi got embroiled in a post-match row with Rodri, saying: 'Start talking less, idiot. You guys spent the whole week crying.

'You spent the whole week crying. You and [Aymeric] Laporte, both of you. That's not how it's done. You were crying to the referees all week, my friend.'

Earlier in the week, Laporte had told Spanish outlet Marca: 'I'm not worried at all about physical play as long as it's part of football.

'If the referee does his job, I have no problem with it. It's true that in recent matches we've seen things that have surprised us, situations that have been allowed to go unpunished.

'Especially with Argentina, which is a team that likes to leave little messages with its challenges.

'That shouldn't be allowed in football, particularly in tournaments of this magnitude, because it can unsettle you and make you lose your composure.

'It's the referee's job to keep those situations under control so the match doesn't get away from him.

'If one or two players are allowed to do whatever they want, the game will become chaotic. Since the beginning of the tournament, we've been a very fair team in that regard.

'We don't go around kicking opponents or making reckless fouls, and I think that's the approach we have to maintain in this match. But, of course, a lot will depend on the officiating.'

Sports.title: The race King Charles wants to win ‘more than anything’, according to Royal trainer’s Mum
Sports.content:
The race King Charles wants to win ‘more than anything’, according to Royal trainer’s Mum

Ciaron Maher’s mother spilled the beans on her trip to Royal Ascot in June when she had lunch at Windsor Castle and got to ride in the royal procession

View 2 Images The Melbourne Cup: one of the biggest races in the world (Image: Getty Images)

King Charles has revealed there is one race he wants to win ‘more than anything else’, according to a royal trainer’s Mum.

The King and Queen inherited the royal racehorse string from the late Queen Elizabeth II who had a lifelong passion for horse racing. Despite questions over the future of the Royal Family’s involvement in horse racing following Queen Elizabeth’s death, the King and Queen have maintained the tradition with a smaller yet effective string.

In 2023 they celebrated their first Royal Ascot winner together when Desert Hero won the King George V Stakes and when the horse contested the St Leger they went to Doncaster to cheer him on.

BHA freezes activity of leading syndicate after members complain they’ve not been paid READ MORE :

They also have a handful of horses based in Australia, including three with top trainer Ciaron Maher.

During Royal Ascot, Maher was invited to Windsor Castle for lunch with the King and Queen and were then given the honour of arriving at the racecourse in a horse drawn carriage as part of the royal procession. His plus-one was his mother Eileen who sat next to King Charles at lunch.

Mrs Maher has now spilled the beans on their conversation, giving an interview in Australia to the SENTrack & RSN’s Giddy Up programme.

View 2 Images Eileen Maher with son Ciaron (right) (Image: Getty Images)

“During the lunch he happened to tell me that the Queen asked him to continue the legacy that she had started of having horses trained in other countries,” she said.

“She told him that it was a way of connecting with those communities and a way of keeping in touch. That is why Charles continued by giving Ciaron three horses to train.”

Maher has two potential stayers, Gilded Water and Aeolian, in his stable which are owned by the King and Queen.

Revealing more of her chat with the King, Eileen went on: “He told me that the race that he wants to win more than anything else is the Melbourne Cup, and if Ciaron could get one of those horses into the Melbourne Cup, he and Queen Camilla would definitely come out for the race.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury drops retirement bombshell ahead of Mariusz Wach fight amid Anthony Joshua plans
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury drops retirement bombshell ahead of Mariusz Wach fight amid Anthony Joshua plans

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are due to fight this year finally - with both returning to the ring this week as part of their preparations for facing each other

View 2 Images Tyson Fury has made clear that his boxing career is now almost over (Image: Getty Images)

Tyson Fury claims this year will be the last of his career. The Gypsy King faces Mariusz Wach in Thailand today and is due to fight Anthony Joshua before the end of 2026.

‌



Fury, 37, retired for the sixth time last January before again reversing that decision barely a year later. The former unified heavyweight world champion returned to the ring after 16 months away in April with a unanimous decision victory over Arslanbek Makhmudov at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

‌



Fury fights Wach a day before Joshua takes on Kristian Prenga, with the British duo expected to face each other later this year. It is Joshua's first bout since last he was involved in a devastating car crash last year, which saw his two close friends Latif Ayodele and Sina Ghami pass away.

‌



Anthony Joshua makes offer to Tyson Fury ahead of mega-fight READ MORE :

New venue emerges for Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury mega-fight READ MORE :

Speaking before his second fight of 2026, Fury told The Sun: "This is my final year. That's why I want to be active. I don't want to go on until I'm 65 years old." He then confirmed: "This is the last year, yeah. Final year, 26."

Fury hinted at a busy autumn and winter, saying: "I just want to keep busy, keep active. It's not about money, it's not about belts, it's about nothing now.

"It's about enjoying my life and enjoying my career and doing what I love to do. That's boxing training, so maybe I'll do quite a lot this year."

‌



View 2 Images Tyson Fury fights Mariusz Wach today

Fury has not fought more than twice in a calendar year since 2018. On that occasion, he was also coming out of retirement, after two-and-a-half years away.

There were two warm-up fights against Francesco Pianeta and Sefer Seferi in the summer before taking on Deontay Wilder. If he is to fight four times in 2026 and rematch Joshua, that would be the first time he has done so since 2011.

‌



Fury was fighting for British and Commonwealth titles at the time, beating Derek Chisora for those two belts. However, one of those bouts was over ten rounds, rather than 12.

He has had only one 10-round fight since then, against Francis Ngannou three years ago. Any bout with Joshua would also presumably not be over anything less than 12 rounds.

Details about the prospective fight are still to be confirmed, with the hope that they will be announced after both of them come through their bouts this week. Turki Al-Sheikh announced in April that Netflix would broadcast it, but a venue remains unconfirmed.

Joshua's promoter has previously said that the contract specifies the United Kingdom. Al-Sheikh acknowledged earlier this month that Wembley Stadium would be his preferred host this month.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp officially named as Germany boss as worst-kept secret in football confirmed
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp officially named as Germany boss as worst-kept secret in football confirmed

Jurgen Klopp has been announced as the new Germany manager, succeeding Julian Nagelsmann following their embarrassment at the hands of Paraguay in the World Cup

View 2 Images Jurgen Klopp has been confirmed as the new Germany manager (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Jurgen Klopp has been officially announced as the new manager of Germany on a four-year contract. The former Liverpool boss will leave his current role with Red Bull to succeed Julian Nagelsmann after his resignation in the wake of a disappointing World Cup.

‌



Klopp was identified as the top target immediately after Nagelsmann stepped down and agreed terms to take over earlier this month. The 59-year-old has been working as Red Bull's global head of soccer for the last 19 months following his departure from Liverpool in 2024, but will now step back into the dugout.

‌



Germany were knocked out of the World Cup in the last 32 by Paraguay, leaving Nagelsmann little choice but to resign the position he'd held since succeeding Hansi Flick in September 2023.

‌



Klopp, who has managed Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool, was in North America following Die Mannschaft as a pundit for German TV, where he was critical of their approach. He stepped down at Liverpool at the end of the 2023/24 season due to fatigue but said earlier this month that he feels "recharged".

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Argentina president goes on rant as calls for country to be banned from World Cup grow READ MORE :

"It is a great honour for me to be here. Over the last few days it has always felt like a movie happening to me," Klopp told a press conference on Friday.

‌



"I’ve always known that the job of Germany head coach is big but now it’s really dawning on me what the job is about. If you look at where I’ve come from it was unimaginable that this job was ever for me. Now I think the time is right and I’m grateful to everyone concerned. Ideally, it is a path that we will all go on together."

It was also confirmed on Friday that Per Mertesacker will take over from Andreas Rettig as the sporting director for the German Football Association. The former Germany defender left his role with Arsenal's academy and will take up the new job in January 2027.

Klopp won the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup and two League Cups during a hugely successful nine-year spell at Liverpool. He also has a stellar reputation in Germany, where he led Dortmund to two Bundesliga titles and the Champions League final.

‌



View 2 Images Julian Nagelsmann resigned after Germany were knocked out of the World Cup (Image: Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

The move has been predicted for some time and has been an anticipated since Klopp publicly confirmed talks at the start of July, while working at the World Cup for a German broadcaster. "Yes, I can confirm the talks," Klopp told Magenta. "Things moved pretty quickly. Julian stepped down. The DFB are looking for a successor and they're talking to me.

"What needs to happen now? Time. I'm under contract with Red Bull. I've said I'm interested in the talks. They will be intensive because this isn't only about Julian Nagelsmann.

Article continues below

"I have an existing contract with Red Bull. I've said many times how much I enjoy this job. As a person, I usually honour contracts. But I've also made it clear that I'm interested in talks with the DFB."

Sports.title: Arsenal can give Bruno Guimaraes perfect sweetener if £70million transfer goes through
Sports.content:
Arsenal can give Bruno Guimaraes perfect sweetener if £70million transfer goes through

Arsenal are stepping up their efforts to sign Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is pressing to join Arsenal (Image: Iain Buist/Newcastle Chronicle)

Arsenal can hand Bruno Guimaraes his cherished squad number if they can get a deal for the Newcastle midfielder over the line. The Brazilian is a top target for the Gunners, with the midfielder eager to join the Premier League champions.

‌



Newcastle are aware of Arsenal's interest but do not want to sell, having let Sandro Tonali join Tottenham for £100million earlier this summer. However, a trend has emerged regarding wanted Newcastle players, with the club initially digging their heels before eventually sanctioning a move.

‌



The Gunners will hope that is the case as they prepare to make a £70m bid for the 28-year-old. Despite their admiration for Guimaraes, they are reportedly unwilling to go beyond that figure.

‌



If Arsenal do sign Guimaraes, they would presumably hand him the number 39 shirt he has routinely worn in club football. He wears that number for a very special reason: it was the number on the taxi his father drove in Brazil.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Guimaraes credits his dad's support and sacrifice for helping him realise his football dreams. He once said: "The number on my shirt tells a story more beautiful than words can express. I know that people think it's a strange number for a footballer.

‌



5 attackers Arsenal could still sign after Morgan Rogers transfer setback READ MORE :

"But for me, the 39 is special. It's magical. The number 39 has given me everything in life. It brought me here to Newcastle. It fed me, clothed me and funded the trips that allowed me to realise my dream of becoming a footballer.

"The number 039 was my father's taxi number in Rio de Janeiro. My father drove that yellow taxi day and night so that I could eat.

"Now, when he walks through the streets of Newcastle, on the other side of the world, people stop him and ask for photos. That yellow taxi kept my dream alive."

‌



View 3 Images Guimaraes has always worn number 39 for his clubs (Image: Iain Buist/Newcastle Chronicle)

Following the unveiling of Arsenal's squad numbers for the new season, the 39 shirt is currently vacant, having belonged to youngster Harrison Dudziak last season. Previously, it has been worn by Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin.

Guimaraes arrived at St James' Park in a £35m switch from Lyon in January 2022 as Amanda Staveley’s consortium opened the purse strings three months after completing their takeover.

‌



View 3 Images Eddie Howe doesn't want to lose Guimaraes (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

Initially nursed into the team by head coach Eddie Howe, he quickly established himself as a fans' favourite and, having been appointed captain, led the Magpies to their first major domestic trophy for 70 years in the 2024-25 Carabao Cup final.

Should he depart, he would leave a sizeable hole in a team already depleted by the departures of Tonali and Anthony Gordon, who has joined Barcelona.

Sports.title: World Cup star allegedly tests positive for cocaine after double police stop
Sports.content:
World Cup star allegedly tests positive for cocaine after double police stop

The Australian international made three appearances for the Socceroos at this summer's tournament.

View 2 Images Cristian Volpato was reportedly stopped twice by police for speeding. (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Australia international Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine after being stopped by police twice in the same night in Sydney. The midfielder represented the Socceroos at this summer's World Cup in North America.

‌



NSW police report that Volpato was stopped for the first time at around 11pm local time for travelling between 86-94km/h in a 60km/h zone. He took a roadside breathalyser, which was negative.

‌



Just a couple of hours later, at around 1am, the 22-year-old in a BMW Coupe was said to have been stopped again after allegedly travelling at 109 km/h on the 60/km/h limited Anzac Bridge. This time, a roadside drug test allegedly returned a positive result for cocaine, with a second sample taken for further analysis.

‌



Argentina president goes on rant as calls for country to be banned from World Cup grow READ MORE :

Man Utd may have to scrap strict Arsenal transfer rule after latest Marcus Rashford blow READ MORE :

Volpato was handed a speeding fine and is reported to have had his international driver's licence suspended for six months, meaning that he is not permitted to drive in New South Wales. He has not been charged with a criminal offence, and the police have confirmed they will continue their enquiries.

The midfielder played three times for Australia during their World Cup campaign. After being an unused substitute for the opening game against Turkey, he featured in the other two group games against the USA and Paraguay, as well as the round of 32 penalty shootout loss vs Egypt.

View 2 Images Cristian Volpato has reportedly tested positive for cocaine.

‌



Volpato switched allegiances to Australia back in May, having represented Italy at youth level. His only international appearance for the nation before the World Cup came in a warm-up match against Switzerland in June.

In a statement, relayed by Australian outlet ABC, Australia football said it "was aware of the allegations involving one of our players."

‌



They added: "We have been in contact with the player and continue to monitor the matter and support the player throughout this process.”

The 22-year-old was born and raised in Sydney, but moved to Italy in 2020 to join Roma's youth system.

He joined fellow Serie A side Sassuolo in 2023, making 26 appearances in all competitions last season.
